title: Senior AI Engineer (all genders)
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer who treats LLMs as production software, not as magic. Someone who can own the agent layer of our platform end to end - from prompt and context design, through tool use and orchestration, to evals, reliability, and continuous improvement in live customer environments.

This role sits at the intersection of two things that are rarely mastered together: shipping LLM-powered systems that actually work in messy enterprise reality, and the discipline of a real engineer - evals, observability, cost, latency, failure modes. Models get smarter every month. What stays scarce is the engineering judgment to make them reliably useful on top of SAP, Oracle, and the mess of real operational data.

You will be a senior individual contributor working directly with the founders. The person in this role won’t be handed a roadmap - they’ll help define it, and build the AI practice around it.

What you will do

AI Ownership

  • Own the agent layer end-to-end: prompt and context design, tool use, orchestration, evals, and long-term technical direction.

  • Be the person who understands why an agent made the decision it made - and who other engineers come to when a model behaves in ways they can’t explain.

  • Set the bar on how we build with LLMs: eval-driven development, context engineering, structured outputs, cost and latency discipline.

  • Make foundational decisions with conviction - which model, which pattern, which guardrail - document the reasoning, and evolve them as the system grows.

LLM Systems in Production

  • Design agents that survive real enterprise environments: ambiguous inputs, flaky upstream systems, exception cases that weren’t in anyone’s spec.

  • Build the eval harness that lets us ship confidently: offline evals, online evals, regression suites, human-in-the-loop review.

  • Think in failure modes: hallucinations, silent drift, prompt injection, tool misuse. Build the detection before you need it.

  • Own cost and latency as first-class product requirements, not afterthoughts.

Agent & Context Engineering

  • Design agent architectures that compose cleanly: tool selection, state, memory, planning, escalation.

  • Build the context layer that makes agents actually useful on top of SAP and Oracle data - retrieval, grounding, schema awareness, auditability.

  • Evolve agents without breaking live customer deployments; manage prompt and model versioning with intention.

  • Know when the right answer is a bigger model, a better prompt, a fine-tune, a tool, or just classical code.

Reliability & Systems Thinking

  • Detect regressions in agent behavior before a customer does; build the evals and observability to catch them early.

  • Own the operational posture of the AI systems you ship: alerting, runbooks, replay, on-call readiness.

  • Identify structural debt in prompts, pipelines, and context before it compounds; refactor with thought.

What we are looking for

  • Experience: 6+ years building production software, with clear ownership of LLM-powered systems in real customer environments - not demos, not notebooks.

  • LLM depth: Non-negotiable. You’ve shipped agents or LLM features that run on live traffic. You have strong opinions about prompting, context, tool use, structured outputs, and what breaks in production.

  • Evals as a first instinct: You don’t ship LLM code without a way to measure it. You’ve built eval pipelines that actually catch regressions, not just vibes.

  • Python depth: You’re fluent in Python and comfortable in production service codebases. You make deliberate calls about async, framework choice, and performance.

  • Reliability instinct: Hallucination containment, idempotency on tool calls, graceful degradation when a model is wrong - part of how you design, not patched in later.

  • End-to-end ownership: You’re comfortable being the person who holds the full agent picture - from prompt to production incident. You identify what’s broken or missing before you’re asked.

  • A real spike: We’re a strong team with broad coverage. What we’re hiring for is someone who brings a 10x improvement in an area we’re currently underinvested in. That might be agent evaluation, context engineering on enterprise data, agentic reliability, deep NLP/LLM internals, or domain-specific grounding. We don’t know exactly what shape it takes - but you should know what yours is, and be able to articulate why it matters.

Kenyon International Emergency Services, part of the TrustFlight Group

Bracknell, United Kingdom | Full time, permanent | Competitive salary and benefits package

When the worst happens, families need someone they can trust. Lead that response.

When an aircraft is lost, a ship is in distress or a community is struck by disaster, families are suddenly facing the hardest days of their lives. They need answers, they need to be treated with dignity, and they need to know that the people they have lost are being cared for. For more than a century, Kenyon International Emergency Services has been the organisation that airlines, governments and major companies call on to make sure that happens.

We are looking for a senior crisis leader to direct that response across the UK, Europe and Africa. This is a role for someone who has stood in the room when it mattered, who leads with calm authority, and who believes that how an organisation treats the bereaved and the injured says everything about its character.

About Kenyon

Kenyon provides emergency planning, family assistance, humanitarian support and recovery services to clients around the world, drawing on a network of more than 2,500 trained responders who can be mobilised at short notice into any jurisdiction. Our clients rely on us to keep their promises to the people affected by an incident, and we hold ourselves to that standard every day, not only on the day of an activation.

Kenyon is part of the TrustFlight Group, an aviation safety and compliance technology business. That gives Kenyon something unusual in this sector: a world class technology team working alongside it, and a genuine commitment to using AI to make crisis response faster, better informed and more humane. Our values are simple and we mean them: integrity, and a customer first attitude in everything we do.

The role

Kenyon operates a two hub leadership model. You will lead the Bracknell hub, with regional accountability for operational delivery, readiness, contracted offices and relationships across the UK, Europe and Africa. Your peer, the Regional Director of Operations in Vancouver, leads the Americas and Asia Pacific. Together you share accountability for the readiness and quality of Kenyon’s response worldwide.

Senior Incident Director for activations

Senior on call duty is shared between the two Directors on a fixed twelve hour rota, with a structured handover at each change of duty, so that cover is continuous around the clock and neither Director works through their own night. Your window runs from approximately 06:00 to 18:00 UK time.

When an incident arises during your window, wherever in the world it occurs, you take up the role of Senior Incident Director. You will have the authority to set the deployment posture, commit responders and stand the organisation up or down without further approval. Where a client requires it, you will deploy as their strategic point of contact, leading the response on their behalf at the most demanding moments an organisation can face, including mass casualty, government led and politically sensitive events.

Major activations are infrequent, and Kenyon holds its capability through a surge based model rather than a large permanent workforce. Your judgement of regional readiness, kept current every week of the year, is what makes that model work.

What you will lead

·       Regional readiness and response. Maintain and continuously measure activation readiness across the UK, Europe and Africa, and develop the procedures, protocols and contingency plans that underpin it.

·       Your team and offices. Line manage the Regional Operations Manager in Bracknell, run the Bracknell hub and its regional operations as one regional function, and hold contracted offices to defined standards through quarterly reviews and an annual assessment.

·       Protecting those we serve. Make sure the information of casualties, families and clients is protected with the same care during and after an activation as on any other day.

·       The responder network. Work with the Responder Manager to keep the network vetted, trained and available across the region, including building language capable responders across Europe and Africa. Own the global standards for responder vetting, training currency, deployment conduct and post incident review, ensuring they are consistently applied across both hubs.

·       AI and digital quality assurance. Work with the Vancouver Director and TrustFlight Group technology team to define and evaluate AI enabled quality and operational reporting tools, including an AI internal auditor supporting ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and ISO 22300 evidence gathering, gap identification and audit trail maintenance. Ensure these tools meet group information security, data governance and ethical standards.

·       Global operational standards. Work with the Vancouver Director to compare regional procedures, share lessons learned and adopt improvements across both hubs, ensuring consistent service quality while recognising regional operational requirements.

·       Relationships that matter. Build trusted working relationships with government agencies, emergency services, aviation authorities and clients across the region, and provide the operational insight that informs board level reporting.

Why join us

·       Work that matters. Few roles offer the chance to lead a service whose sole purpose is to bring order, care and dignity to people at the worst moment of their lives.

·       Real authority. A senior seat on the Kenyon leadership team, reporting to the Managing Director, with decision making authority during activations.

·       A sustainable model. A shared rota designed so that no Director carries standing 24/7 availability, because sound judgement depends on rest.

·       Room to build. The opportunity to shape Kenyon’s growth across the UK, Europe and Africa, while leading the development of global quality, certification and responder standards and helping shape how AI strengthens operational assurance across Kenyon.

In your cover letter, tell us about an incident you have led and what it taught you about caring for the people affected. Applications will be treated in strict confidence.

Kenyon International Emergency Services and TrustFlight are equal opportunity employers. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and will make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process for anyone who needs them. This position is employed by Kenyon International Emergency Services Limited.


What you will bring

·       At least ten years in operational crisis management or emergency response, including five or more in a leadership role.

·       Experience leading large scale or complex incident responses in international environments, ideally including direct responsibility for strategic command.

·       A track record of managing contracted service providers against defined performance standards.

·       Experience working within a quality management framework in a regulated or standards led environment, and alongside board level governance.

·       The composure, judgement and compassion to lead when the stakes are highest, and the humility to put the needs of affected families first.

·       Willingness to travel internationally at short notice, including to the United States and across Asia Pacific.

·       Eligibility to live and work in the UK.

It would be a real advantage if you also have

·       Professional fluency in Spanish, or another principal European and African language.

·       Familiarity with the ISO 22300 series, including ISO 22320, or equivalent certification experience.

·       Experience overseeing a 24/7 contact centre operation.

·       Practical experience commissioning AI or automation tools in an operational setting.

·       Knowledge of the aviation, maritime, energy or government crisis response markets in the Europe and Africa.

description:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

About the Hardware organisation at Fractile
Processor Architecture sits within Fractile’s hardware organisation, which owns everything from compute engine definition and ISA design through memory hierarchies, on-chip interconnects, and the path from early architectural exploration through to tapeout and post-silicon validation. Architecture at Fractile isn’t a paper exercise — it’s built in constant collaboration with logical design, physical design, and verification teams, so that every architectural decision is grounded in what will actually perform in working silicon.

About the team and role
As an Early Career Processor Architect, you’ll join our architecture team to learn how to define the compute engines, ISA definitions and programming models that sit at the heart of our silicon. Working closely with senior architects and our logical design, physical design, and verification teams, you’ll get real exposure to performance modelling, specification writing, bottleneck analysis, and pre- and post-silicon validation — with experienced architects mentoring you as you build toward owning more of this yourself.

About you
We’re looking for someone with a strong foundational understanding of computer or processor architecture — built through coursework, personal projects, internships, placements, or research — who’s genuinely curious about performance and power trade-offs and eager to learn how to navigate them. You don’t need prior industry experience as a Processor Architect; what matters is real hands-on exposure to processor or accelerator design, through a final-year project, FPGA build, RISC-V implementation, internship, or research, plus a comfort working across disciplines and a track record of thriving in ambiguity and fast iteration.

Key Requirements

  • A degree (BEng, MEng, MSc or equivalent) in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.

  • A solid foundational understanding of computer/processor architecture, including matrix- and vector-centric floating-point arithmetic and memory hierarchies, gained through study, projects, internships, or research.

The role

We build the control chain that powers on, monitors, updates, and protects devices and racks across bare metal, RTOS, and embedded Linux. We also build the communication mechanisms that connect devices to each other and to the host. Security runs through all of it. A chain of trust from the hardware up to the rack management plane: the root of trust each controller boots from, the signed updates that reach the fleet safely, the identity that lets a device prove what it is, the authenticated channels the controllers and devices talk over, and the runtime protections that keep the host Linux kernel and the on-die firmware trustworthy long after boot. These are the layers that let operators rely on the hardware.

You’d be deeply involved in that security across the chain, making it real in software. You’ll work hand in hand with our architecture and hardware teams, bringing the software and system-level view: turning threat models into concrete mechanisms in bare metal, RTOS, and Linux, then designing, prototyping, and validating them. Some of the calls in this model are still open, and you’ll help shape them.

We want engineers who understand security from the inside out. You know how the root of trust, boot chain, key hierarchy, and secure interconnects actually work under the hood, not just how to switch them on. In this role, the security of your software solutions depends entirely on how well you understand the hardware beneath it. Some of the protections we rely on live in silicon, some in software, and part of the skill is knowing which belongs where. We’re looking for people who know both sides well enough to build the mechanisms that close whole classes of bugs by design.

We’re not heavy on levels here! Whether you’d call yourself senior, staff, principal, or lead, what matters is depth of security judgement, system-level experience, and working well with the engineers around you. If you’ve worked deep in the security of real systems and like to get your hands on the code and the systems around it, we’d like to hear from you.

What you’ll do:

  • Shape the security of the control chain (device, board, chassis, and rack controllers): threat models, trust boundaries, and a coherent secure-by-design approach across all platforms

  • Design and help build secure boot and the root of trust on each controller: verified/measured boot, signing and verification, anti-rollback, and locking down debug and privileged access in production

  • Secure the interconnects, between controllers and between devices and the host, with authentication, integrity, and additional protections where needed

  • Design and build the cryptographic mechanisms: key hierarchies, provisioning and storage, device identity, and remote attestation so the fleet can prove what it’s running

  • Hands-on experience with the core security primitives in software and in silicon: secure boot, root of trust, cryptography, and key management, including how they’re implemented and where they can fail

  • Secure protocol and channel design between components

  • Strong C and Rust, and the instinct for memory safety and defensive coding that low-level security work needs

  • Experience building, not just using, security mechanisms: a secure-boot chain, key hierarchy, or attestation flow you shaped

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Internship
description:
Le poste

Les Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSE) travaillent directement avec les clients afin de comprendre rapidement leurs problèmes les plus importants et ainsi concevoir et implémenter des solutions qui vont utiliser leurs données afin de résoudre ces problématiques. Nos clients s’appuient sur les plateformes de Palantir pour certaines de leurs opérations les plus critiques, et les projets débutent souvent par une question ouverte, par exemple : « Comment évaluer le risque d’incendie de forêt et, par conséquent, comment optimiser le réseau électrique ? » ou « Comment évaluer rapidement notre chaîne d’approvisionnement alimentaire et l’adapter afin d’apporter à temps une aide vitale ? » En tant que FDSE, vous appliquez votre capacité à résoudre les problèmes, votre créativité et vos compétences techniques pour aider les organisations à exploiter au mieux leurs données et avoir ainsi un impact réel sur le monde. Vous avez l’opportunité d’obtenir des informations rares et de contribuer à certaines des industries et institutions les plus importantes au monde.

Responsabilités principales

En tant que stagiaire chez FDSE, vos responsabilités s’apparentent à celles que l’on trouve dans une petite start-up, tout en bénéficiant des ressources, de la stabilité et de l’accompagnement d’une entreprise technologique bien établie. Vous travaillerez en petites équipes avec une supervision minimale et serez responsable de l’exécution de bout en bout de projets à enjeux élevés. Votre journée peut consister à discuter de l’architecture avec d’autres ingénieurs, à gérer des données à grande échelle, à coder une application web personnalisée, à discuter avec l’équipe dirigeante du client ou à établir une stratégie pour votre équipe.

Les stagiaires FDSE sont traités exactement comme des ingénieurs à temps plein, et bénéficient d’une grande liberté et d’une grande autonomie dans leur travail. Ils assument la responsabilité des projets et des résultats réels sur lesquels nos clients comptent.

Nos principes:
  • Impact : nous gérons des projets significatifs et enthousiasmants qui rendent le monde meilleur.
  • Responsabilité : nous menons nos projets du début à la fin, en surmontant tous les obstacles que nous pourrions rencontrer. Nous nous faisons mutuellement confiance afin de gérer efficacement le temps et les priorités et donner aux individus l’espace nécessaire pour réfléchir par eux-mêmes.
  • Collaboration : nous travaillons en interne avec des personnes d’horizons variés, tels que d’autres FDSE, des équipes Produits et des Deployment Strategists. Nous travaillons également en externe avec nos clients, souvent sur site, afin de comprendre et de répondre à leurs problèmes.
  • Développement : nous pensons que l’apprentissage par l’expérience est l’une des meilleures écoles et nous nous encourageons nous-mêmes tout comme nos pairs à rechercher de nouveaux défis et de nouvelles opportunités de croissance, ainsi qu’à trouver de nouvelles façons d’innover et de partager les connaissances.
Le profil recherché

  • Capacité démontrée à apprendre continuellement, à travailler de manière autonome et à prendre des décisions avec un minimum de direction.
  • Capacité à collaborer avec des équipes de personnes techniques et non techniques, et à être à l’aise pour travailler dans un environnement en évolution constante avec des objectifs dynamiques et des itérations avec les utilisateurs.
  • Volonté de résoudre de façon créative les problèmes techniques liés aux structures de données, aux systèmes de stockage, à l’infrastructure cloud, aux frameworks front-end et à d’autres outils techniques.
  • Intérêt à travailler avec des données à grande échelle et à les utiliser pour résoudre des problèmes opérationnels importants.
Les exigences
  • Expérience en ingénierie, de préférence dans des domaines tels que l’informatique, les mathématiques, le Software Engineering, la physique et la science des données.
  • Maîtrise de langages de programmation tels que Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript ou similaire.
  • Vous devez prévoir d’obtenir votre diplôme en 2027. Il doit s’agir de votre dernier stage avant d’obtenir votre diplôme.
Pour postuler, veuillez soumettre ce qui suit :
  • Un CV à jour
  • Des réponses réfléchies à nos questions de candidature
Date limite de l’offre

Afin de renforcer la transparence de notre processus de recrutement, nous aimerions vous faire part de nos attentes concernant la date limite de l’offre. En postulant à ce poste, vous vous engagez à confirmer votre décision dans les deux semaines suivant la réception de votre offre écrite.

La vie chez Palantir

Nous tenons à ce que chaque Palantirien(ne) atteigne son meilleur potentiel, c’est pourquoi nous célébrons les forces, les compétences et les intérêts des individus, de votre premier entretien à votre croissance à long terme, plutôt que de nous appuyer sur les échelles de carrière traditionnelles. L’attention portée aux besoins de notre communauté nous permet d’optimiser nos possibilités de croissance et contribue à garantir de nombreuses voies de réussite chez Palantir. Promouvoir la santé et le bien-être dans tous les domaines de la vie des Palantiriens n’est que l’une des façons dont nous investissons dans notre communauté. Apprenez-en davantage sur la vie chez Palantir et notez que nos offres peuvent varier selon les régions.

Conformément aux valeurs et à la culture de Palantir, nous estimons que les employés sont « meilleurs ensemble » et que le travail en présentiel permet d’obtenir des résultats plus créatifs. En conséquence, nous encourageons les employés à travailler depuis nos bureaux pour favoriser la connectivité et l’innovation. De nombreuses équipes proposent des options hybrides (télétravail un jour ou deux par semaine), ce qui permet à nos employés de trouver le bon compromis pour leur productivité personnelle. En fonction des besoins de l’entreprise, il existe quelques postes qui permettent de travailler « à distance » de manière exceptionnelle. Si vous postulez à l’un de ces postes, vous devez travailler depuis la ville et/ou le pays dans lequel vous êtes employé(e). Si le poste précise « sur site », vous devez travailler depuis un bureau.

Si vous souhaitez donner aux organisations les plus importantes au monde les moyens d’agir, votre place est ici. Palantir valorise l’excellence, d’où qu’elle vienne. Nous nous engageons à rendre le processus de candidature et d’embauche accessible à tous et offrirons des aménagements raisonnables aux personnes vivant en situation de handicap. Si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement pour le processus de candidature ou d’embauche, veuillez et nous indiquer comment nous pouvons vous aider.

Attention : il ne vous sera jamais demandé d’envoyer un paiement ou de partager des données financières pour participer à notre processus d’entretien. Si vous pensez avoir été contacté par un escroc, nous vous conseillons de cesser toute communication avec la personne et d’envisager de la signaler aux autorités compétentes, telles que l’Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) du FBI aux États-Unis.

A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

 

The Role

Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations, and projects often start with an open-ended question like, "How do we evaluate wildfire risk and optimise a power grid as a result" or "How do we quickly assess our food supply chain and modify it to deliver life saving assistance on time?" As an FDSE, you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organisations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the world’s most important industries and institutions. 

Core Responsibilities

As an FDSE Intern, your responsibilities look similar to those at a small startup, with the resources, stability and mentorship of an established tech company. You’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team.

FDSE Interns are treated just like full time engineers, with significant freedom and ownership over their work. Interns take responsibility for real world projects and outcomes that our customers rely on.

Our Principles:

  • Impact: We address meaningful and exciting projects that change the world for the better.

  • Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter. We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves.

  • Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other FDSEs, product teams, and Deployment Strategists. We also work externally with our customers, often on site, to understand and tackle their problems.

title: Product Manager
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

At Loft, we are convinced that space programs should not have to be rebuilt from scratch every time. Our philosophy has been to productize them: we develop our own proprietary technology blocks, hardware and software, so that a customer payload can be integrated faster and more reliably than any bespoke program allows. That approach has delivered — it is why our customers reach orbit in months rather than years, and it is what makes working here different from working in the rest of the industry.

We are now taking the next step: launching and operating our own constellations, and building a new set of services on top of them. That includes a full product suite enabling third-party AI applications to run directly onboard our satellites, and a growing ecosystem of partners whose needs we have to understand and design for. Loft is expanding at a very high pace, and the range of what we build is expanding just as fast.

This is why Product Management matters so much here. Someone has to hold the whole picture — what is technically possible, what customers actually need, what we should build first — and turn it into something engineering and leadership can act on. As a Product Manager, you will own a significant perimeter and the autonomy that goes with it. We are growing the team precisely so that each of us can go deeper on our topics, anticipate rather than react, and have more impact across the company.

You will need to be comfortable talking to anyone here. In the same week you might sit with a system engineer to understand a design constraint, join a BD call with an institutional customer, and present a recommendation to the executive team. Ideas at Loft get discussed openly and on their merits, wherever they come from, so being able to ask a naive question without ego — and to disagree with someone senior without making it personal — matters more than seniority.


About this role:
Understand what is possible, and turn it into requirements
  • Spend the bulk of your time with engineering: understanding architectures, constraints, and dependencies well enough to judge what is realistically doable in a given timeframe.
  • Translate strategic direction into clear requirements and use cases that engineering can act on directly, and follow them down to the Jira tickets.
  • Surface and shape the good ideas that come from engineering — many of the best ones do — and connect them to a product rationale.

    • Bring the outside in

    • Engage directly with the partners building on our platform, including the onboard AI application ecosystem, to understand their needs and constraints.
    • Track market trends and competitive moves closely enough to know where our offering stands.

      • Decide and prioritize

      • Build the analysis behind every recommendation — sizing, segmentation, business cases, operational data — so decisions are grounded in evidence rather than intuition alone.
      • Negotiate scope and delivery commitments with engineering leadership, and re-plan when capacity or mission timelines shift.
      • Challenge, constructively and with data, business development, engineering leadership, and your own assumptions.

        • Communicate

        • Develop the technical narratives and proof points that marketing and BD then turn into their own customer-facing material.

  • Structured and data-driven: you bring your experience and your intuitions, but when you put a recommendation on the table you can show the analysis it stands on.
  • Real product obsession: you think about the bigger picture and product-market fit before you think about features.

title: Onboard Software Engineer - Deployment & Runtime Environments
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft’s Onboard Software group provides the on-orbit software that powers our satellite fleet — from the Linux services running on the hub processor, to the containerized workloads executing customer applications in low Earth orbit.

The Deployment & Runtime Environments team is where software meets the satellite. We own how software gets packaged, deployed, and executed onboard: from the tool that assembles and maintains mission-specific software stacks, to the Runtime Container Environment that lets partner and customer workloads run securely in orbit, to the Linux infrastructure that makes it all reliable. As more satellite programs come online and as we open our container runtime to a growing number of external workloads, the team’s scope is expanding fast.

We’re looking for someone scrappy — the kind of engineer who digs into an unfamiliar system, maps it out, and gets it shipped without needing the path handed to them. You’ll move between Linux internals, container runtimes, and CI pipelines, sometimes in the same afternoon.


About this role:
  • Contribute to and evolve our bundle management tool — the tool that resolves package dependencies, assembles mission-specific software stacks, and enables the Solutions team to spin up and maintain an ever-growing number of satellite programs
  • Develop and harden our onboard Linux infrastructure: how services are deployed on the rootfs, what system manages their execution, and how we ensure reliable and recoverable Linux operation in orbit
  • Evolve our Runtime Container Environment — the container manager and the full stack around it (base images, container registry service) — enabling partner and customer workloads to run securely onboard our vehicles
  • Support scaling of the deployment pipeline as new hardware platforms are added and the number of active satellite programs grows
  • Contribute to Product Validation — as the last step in the development pipeline, the team plays a key role in validating software readiness before it goes to orbit

title: Principal Thermal Solutions Engineer - Paris/Grenoble
description:
Principal Thermal Solutions Engineer – Paris/Grenoble

About Vinci

We are building Physics AI for hardware design. Our software platform helps hardware designers and physics simulation engineers explore, analyze, and optimize hardware systems, leveraging cutting-edge AI to deliver ultrafast, accurate physics intelligence within the realities of engineering design workflows.

Our first product bridges the gap between the accuracy and determinism of traditional simulation and the speed and scaling of AI, and is redefining how the world's most advanced semiconductors are designed, verified, built, brought to market, and integrated into complex systems.

Role Overview

As a pivotal leader within our European technical sales team, you will drive the adoption of Vinci's platform among the region's top engineering organizations. In this strategic role, you will build, mentor, and guide a high-performing team of thermal engineers dedicated to engaging prospective customers and demonstrating the transformative value of our software.

By acting as trusted technical advisors, you and your team will use deep simulation expertise to help enterprise customers validate and optimize complex, real-world designs. Through these collaborative engagements, you will champion Vinci's value proposition, showcasing how our platform delivers systemic improvements in thermal performance, product reliability, and accelerated time-to-market.

Leveraging strong fundamentals in thermal physics and cooling strategies, you will guide analyses of complex thermal management systems, fluid flow dynamics, and heat dissipation challenges, including both steady-state and transient thermal behavior. Your team will help customers evaluate critical factors such as thermal risk, component reliability, power density, and cooling efficiency to architect cutting-edge thermal management systems for next-generation hardware.

You will work closely with customer engineering teams to understand their technical challenges, provide expert guidance, and clearly articulate Vinci's capabilities in solving real-world problems. You will also serve as a key feedback channel to product and engineering teams, translating customer insights into actionable inputs that shape product direction and drive continuous improvement.

This is a remote role, with close collaboration with Sales, Product, and Engineering in Palo Alto, CA, USA. The role includes moderate travel, primarily within continental Europe. Some infrequent intercontinental travel may be required for discussions and collaboration with the US team.

Responsibilities

  • Build, lead, and scale a high-performing team of thermal engineers, setting the technical direction, hiring, mentoring team members, and driving field execution across Europe.

  • Collaborate closely with the sales team to lead technical discussions, scope proof-of-concept (PoC) evaluations, and deliver compelling product demonstrations to prospective enterprise customers.

  • Guide customer engineering teams through the evaluation phase by overseeing simulation setup, running complex test cases, and interpreting results to explicitly prove Vinci's technical and business value.

  • Own customer enablement through onboarding, deployment pipeline, and account expansion, providing senior technical guidance, structured training sessions, and advanced troubleshooting.

  • Provide product guidance and feedback, identify customer pain points and workflow bottlenecks, and partner directly with internal product and engineering teams to transform field feedback into critical new product features.

  • Represent Vinci at major industry conferences and semiconductor events, engaging technically with key prospects and partners through technical presentations and live platform demonstrations.

  • Maintain a strong understanding of competitive technologies, industry trends, and market positioning to communicate Vinci's differentiators effectively.

Qualifications (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Education: Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field.

  • Technical depth: Expert-level mastery of commercial simulation software (Flotherm, Ansys Icepak/Fluent, Simcenter STAR-CCM+, or equivalent), with 15+ years of hands-on experience in thermal management and cooling solutions, either as a practitioner running simulations or as a technical account manager for commercial physics simulation software.

  • Industry domain: Deep familiarity with semiconductor electronics packaging, advanced packaging technologies (e.g., 2.5D/3D IC), or foundry ecosystems.

  • Customer engagement: Prior experience in dedicated customer-facing roles, with a strong ability to build trust and manage engineering client relationships.

  • Automation & scripting: Practical programming experience using Python or C++ to automate workflows or parse simulation data.

  • Leadership impact: Proven track record of prior managerial or technical leadership experience, with the ability to scale, mentor, and drive execution across engineering teams.

  • Communication: Elite interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex physics and simulation results into clear, high-impact narratives for both deep technical panels and business-oriented executives.

Preferred (Desirable Differentiators)

  • Multiphysics breadth: Familiarity with structural mechanical simulations (FEA/stress) and/or Electrical Signal Integrity and Power Integrity (SI/PI) workflows.

  • Commercial track record: Direct experience commercializing technical software, ideally electronic design automation (EDA) or CAE simulation tools, into major semiconductor and electronics enterprises.

  • Go-to-market experience: Prior experience within technical pre-sales, application engineering (FAE), or strategic technical sales environments.

  • Emerging tech adjacency: Ability to rapidly adopt and champion next-generation, physics-based workflows and AI-assisted design or simulation tools.

Why Join Us

  • Don't just use AI; help redefine how next-generation hardware is designed.

  • Work at the convergence of state-of-the-art AI models, fundamental physics, and high-stakes enterprise engineering.

  • Collaborate with world-class engineers and researchers in a fast-moving startup environment.

 
 

À propos de Vinci

Vinci développe une IA fondée sur la physique (Physics AI) pour la conception de systèmes hardware. Notre plateforme donne aux équipes de conception et de simulation des prédictions physiques précises, obtenues en une fraction du temps d'une simulation classique, et qui s'intègrent à leurs outils existants.

C'est la première solution à offrir à la fois la rigueur de la simulation traditionnelle et la vitesse de l'IA. Elle transforme la façon dont les semi-conducteurs les plus avancés au monde sont conçus, vérifiés et mis en production.

 

Présentation du poste

En tant que membre clé de notre équipe européenne de Forward Deployment, vous jouerez un rôle déterminant dans l’adoption de la plateforme Vinci par les principales organisations d’ingénierie de la région. Dans ce rôle stratégique, vous constituerez, accompagnerez et dirigerez une équipe performante de spécialistes en ingénierie thermique, chargée d’accompagner nos clients et prospects et de démontrer concrètement la valeur de notre logiciel.

En tant que référent technique de confiance auprès de nos clients, vous et votre équipe mettrez à profit votre expertise approfondie en simulation pour aider nos clients industriels à valider et optimiser des conceptions complexes dans des conditions représentatives de leurs applications réelles. À travers ces collaborations, vous démontrerez comment la plateforme Vinci permet d’améliorer les performances thermiques et la fiabilité des produits, tout en accélérant les cycles de conception et la mise sur le marché.

Grâce à votre solide maîtrise de la physique thermique et des stratégies de refroidissement, vous guiderez l’analyse de systèmes complexes de gestion thermique, notamment les phénomènes de transfert de chaleur, d’écoulement des fluides et de dissipation thermique, en régime permanent comme transitoire. Votre équipe aidera les clients à évaluer des paramètres critiques tels que les risques thermiques, la fiabilité des composants, la densité de puissance et l’efficacité des solutions de refroidissement, afin de concevoir des systèmes de gestion thermique performants pour les équipements de nouvelle génération.

Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d’ingénierie de nos clients afin de comprendre leurs problématiques techniques, de leur apporter une expertise approfondie et de démontrer clairement comment Vinci peut répondre à leurs cas d’usage concrets. Vous jouerez également un rôle essentiel d’interface entre les clients et nos équipes Product et Engineering, en transformant les retours du terrain en informations exploitables pour orienter la feuille de route produit et contribuer à l’amélioration continue de la plateforme.

Ce poste est basé en France et exercé en télétravail, avec une collaboration étroite avec les équipes Sales, Product et Engineering basées à Palo Alto, en Californie. Il implique des déplacements réguliers mais modérés, principalement en Europe continentale, ainsi que des déplacements occasionnels aux États-Unis pour collaborer avec l’équipe américaine

 

Responsabilités

  • Construire, diriger et développer une équipe performante d’ingénieur·es thermiques, en définissant l’orientation technique, en recrutant et accompagnant les membres de l’équipe, et en pilotant l’exécution sur le terrain à travers l’Europe.

  • Collaborer étroitement avec l’équipe Sales pour diriger les discussions techniques, définir le périmètre des évaluations en proof-of-concept (PoC) et réaliser des démonstrations produits convaincantes auprès de clients industriels potentiels.

  • Accompagner les équipes d’ingénierie des clients pendant la phase d’évaluation en supervisant la mise en place des simulations, l’exécution de cas de test complexes et l’interprétation des résultats afin de démontrer concrètement la valeur technique et business de Vinci.

title: Team Lead - Platform Engineering
description:
About the role:


We are looking for a new team lead for one of the teams within our Infra Platform Group. Your mission in this role is to architect and deliver foundational services that empower the product engineering teams building our e-commerce platform.

Together with your team, you will be tackling challenging engineering problems, working on high-performing and scalable services written in Haskell and Rust, while also providing a high-quality developer experience for the teams that use them via Python.


Your time will be split approximately 50-50 between leadership tasks and hands-on development. In your leadership role, you are a mentor to your team members, unblocking them when they face challenging roadblocks, and you help them grow both their hard and soft skills. As part of your hands-on work, you are contributing to the architecture and the ongoing development and maintenance of our services.

You will initially be managing a team of four experienced Haskell and Rust engineers, and you will be working closely together with the other teams in the group, the engineering manager of the Infra Platform Group, and the stakeholders from other engineering teams that consume our services.

If you don't have direct experience with Haskell, but you have solid experience with Rust or Scala and a willingness to learn Haskell, please submit your application, as we are still happy to consider it!

Your responsibilities:

Your Team Lead tasks will include:

  • Organizing the work and managing priorities

  • Collaborating with the other team leads in the Infra Platform Group on the long-term roadmap

  • Mentoring team members, helping them grow and holding half-yearly performance reviews with them

  • Setting up project teams and mentor project leads

  • Hiring new team members

  • Implementing and improving upon our processes for the team 

  • Establishing the team culture and fostering a collaborative environment

Your Development tasks will include:

  • Designing, developing and testing new features in our services

  • Improving the reliability and robustness of our application

  • Working on scalability and performance improvements

  • Collaborating with and review PRs of other engineers

  • Breaking down big projects into smaller issues

  • Writing clear and actionable issues

  • Debugging and fixing issues, and teaching team members to do the same

  • Working together with our product engineering teams and DevOps team on requirements and issues


Who are you?

You like working in a dynamic team of skilled engineers, discussing technical decisions openly and collaboratively. It is easy for you to break down big issues into smaller tasks and to prioritize work pragmatically.

To set you up for success in this role, we think you'll benefit from having the following skills and experience:

  • You have previous experience leading an engineering team, or you are an experienced engineer, excited to start your career as a leader.

  • You can give detailed code reviews both from a high-level and a low-level perspective.

  • You have the technical depth to help your team members grow and can remove roadblocks for them.

  • You have substantial backend development experience, you are experienced with functional programming concepts, and are comfortable working with either Haskell, Scala, or Rust. Experience with Python is a plus.

  • You are familiar with relational databases (ideally PostgreSQL), Linux and git.

  • You have experience with web development, web technologies, and APIs

  • You have strong communication and problem-solving skills

  • You are a people-oriented individual who helps others with an open and approachable attitude.

  • You value high software engineering standards.

  • You are pragmatic and empathic towards your team members and other stakeholders (i.e. colleagues from other departments etc).

  • You like helping the team focus on the most important tasks, making sure its priorities and plans align with the rest of the company (we use the OKR framework for this).

Practical requirements:

  • EU citizenship or a valid work permit for the Netherlands; you are preferably already living in the Netherlands

  • Available for at least 32 hours a week, with two days spent at the Utrecht office

Important note: We understand that studies show women may only apply for roles when they feel they meet 100% of the requirements; therefore, we strongly encourage you to apply even if you don't check every box, as we are looking for passionate individuals with potential and a willingness to grow.

Who are we?

Channable was founded in 2014 in the heart of Utrecht and is a fast-growing B2B SaaS platform that offers a fully integrated way to market your products online. We empower marketers and online businesses to manage, scale, and optimize their marketing. We are now a strong team of 320+ diverse individuals from more than 40+ nationalities.

Joining Channable means you’re looking for a bit more than just a job. Diverse as we are, we all share our love for growth, to help, to take ownership, and create an awesome journey together. Feel free to take a further look at who we are here and on our Instagram or LinkedIn! Wanna get to know us even more? Give our Culture Playbook a read.

Why Channable?

At Channable, you’ll find a culture that values openness, craftsmanship, and collaboration. We invest in our people and give them the autonomy to drive meaningful change. You'll work on technical challenges that matter, with colleagues who care deeply about the product and each other.


What do we offer?

  • Gross annual salary ranging from € 77k-103k, including 8% holiday allowance and based on a 40-hour work week. This salary range reflects our career framework. Your final role level will be determined throughout the recruitment process, based on alignment with this framework.

  • Savings for old age: we have a savings scheme for old age, which can accrue up to 5% of your monthly salary, or you can get an additional +2.5% to your monthly base salary.

  • Annual L&D budget of €1000 to spend on your professional growth.

  • Stock Appreciation Rights: you can profit from Channable’s success.

  • Company-wide performance bonus, up to 10% of your annual salary, determined yearly by our founders based on financial planning and targets.

  • 26 vacation days + 2 reload days based on 40 hours, with the possibility of buying up to 5 extra vacation days per year.

  • Are you going to become a parent? Enjoy 5 weeks of 100% paid partner leave!

  • Commuting to our office? Choose between an NS Business Card or a €0.25/km travel allowance for alternative transport. 

  • Work from our office in central Utrecht at least 2 days a week, and from home for the rest (we'll provide the gear and a budget for extra supplies). Plus, enjoy flexible working hours with a morning start window between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM. 

  • We offer a 3-week-long workcation; and an additional 3 weeks if you live as an expat in the Netherlands!

  • Your well-being matters: we offer a discounted Urban Sports Club subscription and anonymous access to OpenUp psychologists and resources.

  • Fresh daily lunch: enjoy fresh meals prepared Monday to Thursday by our in-house Chef (fully catering to vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free diets). On Fridays, we switch it up by ordering in tasty sandwiches and salads.

  • Additional working conditions include massages, even personal training sessions at our Channagym, video games, an in-office bar, and many more!

  • Channaweek & Channaweekend: connect with your global colleagues at our annual team gathering in Utrecht, and pack your bags for Channaweekend, our annual company-wide getaway. 

How can you introduce yourself to us?
Are you interested? To ensure your application reaches the right team quickly, please submit it in English directly through our careers page by clicking the “Apply” button. Applications submitted via email won’t be considered.
If it's a match, Ioana (Tech Talent Acquisition Partner) will get in touch with you for an introductory call. After that, you'll be invited for interviews. We look forward to hearing from you as soon as possible!

Contact by job agencies and recruiters will not be appreciated. Each recruiter or headhunter who approaches us agrees with a donation of €250 for Make-A-Wish.

At Channable, we strive to create and foster an environment of belonging and collaboration and we believe in diverse and inclusive teams.

title: Marketing Afstudeerstage
description:
Ben jij onze toekomstige Marketeer?

Wij vertellen enterprise-klanten al jaren hetzelfde: dat content zonder structuur niet schaalt. Onze eigen marketing heeft dat fundament nog niet. Bouw jij dat met ons mee?

Over Twentyseven

Wij bouwen content platforms voor enterprise-organisaties die wereldwijd opereren. Steeds vaker bouwen we ook de laag erboven: orchestration, content intelligence en governance. Denk aan Haskoning met zo'n 6.000 engineers wereldwijd, TIAS Business School en Itho Daalderop. Het zijn organisaties waar content dagelijks door tientallen markten en tijdzones reist. 

We zitten in Eindhoven en zijn onderdeel van Handpicked: 11 bureaus en zo'n 300 collega's. We zijn drie keer uitgeroepen tot Best Agency in Digital Development (Emerce100), waarvan twee jaar op rij! Het team bestaat uit engineers, architects en strategen. We zijn direct, kritisch op ons eigen werk en niet onder de indruk van hiërarchie. Een goed argument wint hier altijd van een functietitel. 

Wat de stage inhoudt 

Naast je afstudeeronderzoek werk je mee in de dagelijkse praktijk om de marktpositie van Twentyseven verder te versterken: 

  • Marketing Workflows & Automation: Je bouwt en optimaliseert geautomatiseerde marketingprocessen (van contentcreatie tot posting en opvolging) met behulp van moderne AI-tools. 

  • Contentcreatie & Thought Leadership: Je schrijft en redigeert scherpe B2B-content die onze expertise claimt. 

  • Website & Conversion Optimization: Je analyseert (o.a. via Google Analytics) de performance van onze website en optimaliseert de content voor betere conversie. 

  • Sales & Partner Marketing: Je helpt bij het verbinden van marketing met onze outbound salesactiviteiten en bouwt samenwerkingen met partners verder uit. 

  • Bureaucoördinatie: Je werkt samen met en coördineert de opdrachten naar de interne zusterbureaus binnen Handpicked die ons ondersteunen op creatief en visueel vlak. 

  • Events & Fundament: Je helpt mee bij het organiseren van relatie-events en legt richtlijnen vast voor onze Tone of Voice en marketingguidelines. 


Dit is onze ideale Marketingstagiair: 

  • Je volgt een HBO-opleiding in de richting van Marketing, Communicatie, Digital Business, Commerciële Economie of een gerelateerde studierichting; 

  • Je hebt uitstekende copywriting- en redactievaardigheden in het Nederlands (en bij voorkeur Engels); 

  • Je bent nieuwsgierig naar AI-tools en weet hoe je deze praktisch kunt inzetten voor marketingefficiëntie; 

  • Je hebt affiniteit met data en analyse (kennis van Google Analytics is een pré) om beslissingen te onderbouwen; 

  • Je kunt 'uitzoomen': je kijkt niet alleen naar een losse post, maar begrijpt hoe marketing bijdraagt aan de strategische doelen van een B2B-organisatie; 

  • Je werkt zelfstandig, neemt initiatief en durft kritische vragen te stellen. 


De realiteit

  1. De doelgroep. Je schrijft voor CMO’s en CTO’s van grote organisaties. Ze zijn sceptisch en druk, en hebben al te veel AI-keynotes gezien. Oppervlakkige content valt bij hen direct door de mand.

  2. De organisatie. Je werkt tussen directie, projectmanagement, sales en een extern creatief team. Je leert afstemmen, prioriteren en voet bij stuk houden.

  3. Het fundament. Wat jij neerzet, gebruiken wij na je stage nog steeds. Dat vraagt om keuzes die je kunt uitleggen en documentatie die anderen begrijpen.

Wat wij bieden

  • De praktische kant. Je krijgt €400 per maand. Je komt werken in de hub in Eindhoven, met mogelijkheid om hybride te werken. Je bent voor 32-40 uur per week beschikbaar.

  • Een afstudeeropdracht die blijft staan. Wat jij bouwt, gebruiken we na je stage nog. Je scriptie beschrijft dus iets wat echt draait, en geen casus die na je presentatie in een la verdwijnt.

  • Begeleiding van dichtbij. O.a. onze algemeen directeur en onze senior projectmanager begeleiden je. De lijnen zijn kort, je krijgt regelmatig feedback en we zijn eerlijk, ook als dat even schuurt.

  • Ruimte om te experimenteren. Je krijgt toegang tot onze AI-tooling en mag die loslaten op onze eigen marketing. Als iets niet werkt, leren we daar allebei van.

  • Direct contact met de doelgroep. Je bent erbij als we executive events organiseren. Daar hoor je uit eerste hand wat directeuren van grote organisaties echt bezighoudt, en dat leer je niet uit een marketingboek.

  • Een groot netwerk achter een klein team. Twentyseven is onderdeel van Handpicked: 11 bureaus en zo’n 300 collega’s. Je werkt samen met Weekend en kunt kennis halen bij specialisten in het hele digitale vakgebied.

title: AI platform engineer
description:
Wil jij werken op het snijvlak van cloud, platform engineering en AI? Bij Itility krijg je de ruimte om te bouwen aan een platform dat onze engineers en klantenteams helpt slimmer, efficiënter en veiliger te werken. Je ontwikkelt niet alleen nieuwe functionaliteiten, maar denkt ook actief mee over hoe we AI en automation kunnen inzetten om onze dienstverlening verder te verbeteren.


Wat jij gaat doen

Je bouwt mee aan de verdere ontwikkeling van ons platform en vertaalt behoeften vanuit onze klantenteams naar concrete, herbruikbare oplossingen. Je werkt aan features vanuit de roadmap, maar signaleert ook zelf waar verbeteringen mogelijk zijn.

Een belangrijk onderdeel van je werk is het toepassen van AI en automation. Je ontwikkelt bijvoorbeeld AI-agents die informatie verzamelen en analyseren, engineers ondersteunen bij troubleshooting of binnen duidelijke kaders zelfstandig acties uitvoeren. Je zorgt ervoor dat deze oplossingen niet bij een proof of concept blijven, maar daadwerkelijk in productie worden gebruikt.

Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:

  • Het ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van nieuwe platformfunctionaliteiten.

  • Het doorontwikkelen van onze centrale dashboard- en beheeromgeving.

  • Het bouwen van AI-agents, agentic workflows, API's en integraties.

  • Het ontwikkelen en verbeteren van Terraform-modules en andere automatiseringen.

  • Het inrichten van human-in-the-loop-processen, approvals en guardrails.

  • Het analyseren en automatiseren van terugkerende operationele werkzaamheden.

  • Het ondersteunen bij incidenten, troubleshooting en wijzigingen wanneer dat nodig is.

Je krijgt de ruimte om zelf verbeterkansen te signaleren, ideeën uit te werken en oplossingen te realiseren. Daarbij houd je altijd rekening met security, betrouwbaarheid en beheersbaarheid.

Waar kom je terecht?

Je maakt deel uit van het Platform Team binnen onze MSP-organisatie. Dit team ontwikkelt en beheert de centrale diensten waarop onze klantenteams vertrouwen. Het platform vormt de basis voor onze cloud-, data- en AI-dienstverlening en helpt engineers om hun werk efficiënt, veilig en consistent uit te voeren.

Binnen het team werken we met onder andere:

  • Microsoft Azure en AWS voor cloud-, data- en AI-foundations.

  • Terraform voor Infrastructure as Code en herbruikbare infrastructuurmodules.

  • LogicMonitor voor centrale monitoring.

  • Puppet voor configuration management.

  • Centrale dashboards en tooling voor het beheer en de ontsluiting van onze platformdiensten.

We blijven investeren in de verdere ontwikkeling van dit platform. Daarbij willen we AI en automation een steeds grotere rol geven, zodat onze engineers minder tijd kwijt zijn aan repetitieve werkzaamheden en meer ruimte hebben voor complexe vraagstukken en innovatie.


Daar hoort natuurlijk ook een aantrekkelijk arbeidsvoorwaardenpakket bij. Naast een salaris dat past bij jouw ervaring, achtergrond en potentie, kun je rekenen op:

  • Een Leaseauto met tankpas of een mobiliteitsvergoeding met kilometervergoeding;

  • €115 onkostenvergoeding per maand;

  • 26 vakantiedagen per jaar;

  • 50% bijdrage aan je ziektekostenverzekering van jou én die van je partner;

  • 60% bijdrage aan je pensioenregeling;

  • Een variabele bonusregeling gebaseerd op jouw persoonlijke ontwikkeling en gezamenlijke successen;

title: Web & Mobile Full Stack Developer
description:
The mission
Help build fair, engaged and high-performing teams.
We believe everyone deserves a fair opportunity to develop and be rewarded for the value they bring. That’s why we build software that helps organizations set clear expectations, define what a role entails, assess performance fairly, support employee growth, and make compensation transparent and explainable. From clear roles to fair rewards, all within one continuous process. Will you join us in driving this change?

Please note: for this role, it’s important that you already live in the Netherlands and are able to work from our Utrecht office at least three days a week.

The opportunity
As our new Web & Mobile Full Stack Developer, you’ll help build and improve our SaaS platform across all surfaces: mobile, web and backend. You’ll work on our React Native mobile app as we scale it into a fully independent experience for mobile-first markets. You’ll contribute just as actively to our web platform, from intuitive user interfaces in React to scalable APIs and backend services in Node.js.

Your average week in Utrecht:

  • Building and shipping new features in our React Native mobile app (around 50% of your time)

  • Building and shipping new features on our web platform, with React on the frontend and Node.js on the backend (around 50% of your time)

  • Shaping features together with product and design to improve the user experience

  • Working in structured weekly sprints with your team

  • Writing clean, scalable and maintainable code in TypeScript, React, React Native, Node.js and MongoDB

  • Building and improving performant, secure REST APIs

  • Contributing to technical discussions and architecture decisions, including our mobile strategy

  • Reviewing pull requests to keep quality high

  • Improving developer workflows, CI/CD and automated testing

  • Owning features from idea to deployment, across mobile and web

In short: your work directly makes our platform faster, smarter and more scalable, helping our customers grow and pushing Learned to the next level 🌱

The team
You’ll join a development team of 6 developers in Utrecht, working closely with 11 colleagues in Sri Lanka through a buddy system that keeps lines short. The team is led by Alex, our CTO. We’re an international company of 55 people (7+ nationalities) serving 350+ customers, increasingly at enterprise level. With the EU Pay Transparency Directive coming up, demand for our product is growing fast, and so is our roadmap.

Your growth

  • Learning every day from experienced, senior colleagues across mobile, web and backend

  • Hands-on experience building AI features into a product used by hundreds of companies

  • A personal development budget of €1,000 per year

  • An open feedback culture: we practice what we preach


The musts

  • You already live in the Netherlands and can work from our Utrecht office at least 3 days a week

  • Around 3+ years of experience as a Full Stack Developer

  • At least 1 year of experience building production apps in React Native

  • Solid experience with TypeScript, React and Node.js (or comparable stacks), including REST APIs

  • Experience building or integrating AI features in a product (e.g. LLM features, agents or retrieval)

  • You enjoy switching between mobile, frontend and backend, and owning features end-to-end

  • You communicate clearly and confidently in English

  • You’re proactive, take ownership and love learning together through feedback


The nice-to-haves

  • Experience with MongoDB or similar databases

  • Experience with CI/CD, automated testing and cloud infrastructure

  • Experience publishing apps to the App Store and Google Play

  • Experience in B2B SaaS, ideally HR tech

The benefits

  • A salary between €4,000 and €5,500 gross per month (based on 40 hours, depending on experience), with room to grow

  • 25 vacation days (based on full-time)

  • A pension plan (10%, of which we pay 50%)

  • A personal development budget of €1,000 per year (based on full-time)

  • A MacBook Pro and everything you need to do your job well

  • Travel expense reimbursement via our mobility plan

  • A hybrid setup: at least 3 days at the office, flexible beyond that

  • The option to work remotely from abroad for up to 6 weeks per year

description:

Als Project Engineer begeleid je projecten binnen AEP Hybrid Power vanaf de technische overdracht na opdracht tot en met de oplevering. Jij bent de verbindende schakel tussen de klant, engineering, productiepartners, leveranciers en service.

Binnen AEP zijn we actief in verschillende technische markten, waaronder hybride energie. Met AEP Hybrid Power richten we ons op innovatieve oplossingen op het gebied van energieopslag en vermogenselektronica.

• Enkele jaren relevante werkervaring is mooi meegenomen. Ben je een sterke starter met passende stages of projecten? Ook dan komen we graag met je in gesprek
• Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Duits is een pré

• Je bent technisch analytisch en weet complexe vraagstukken te vertalen naar duidelijke acties

• Je bent proactief, oplossingsgericht en wacht niet af wanneer er actie nodig is

Binnen AEP kom je terecht in een technische en groeiende organisatie waar je veel ruimte krijgt voor eigen inbreng. Je krijgt de mogelijkheid om mee te werken aan innovatieve projecten binnen de energietechniek en jezelf verder te ontwikkelen.

You will create big, viral campaigns, online and offline, that put the everyday people who start petitions on Change.org at the centre of the national conversation. The job also involves being the public voice of Change.org in the German media. You will lead a small, high-performing team, open doors through an exceptional network, and use AI to move faster than anyone else in the news cycle.

We'd welcome ambitious Communications Manager level candidates with leadership presence, who are ready to step up into a team leadership role.

Change.org is the world's largest petition platform, used by more than 100 million people every year to take part in civic life and democracy. At a time when dissatisfaction with democracy is at an all-time high, we are investing heavily in AI to build the most powerful tools in the world to give people a voice, while bringing people across the political spectrum together around shared solutions.

What you will achieve

  • Create awareness spikes. Regularly turn petitions from Change.org petition starters into national moments that people talk about, through viral campaigns that combine top-tier media, social media, video, creators and offline actions such as stunts, petition handovers and public events.

  • Put petition starters in the spotlight. Find the strongest stories and the most credible, unexpected voices, and give them the visibility they need to win.

  • Earn trust across the political spectrum. Make sure Change.org campaigns speak to people across the democratic political spectrum, and protect the trust in our brand as the team moves fast with AI. At a Senior Manager level, build balance checks into how the team works.

  • Mobilise your network. Use and grow high-trust relationships with senior editors, producers, journalists, politicians, decision makers, civil society and creators to secure top-tier coverage and move decision makers.

  • Be our voice. Act as Change.org's external spokesperson in Germany on TV, radio, in print and on stage, representing a trusted, open platform for people across the democratic political spectrum, including in sensitive and crisis situations.

  • Lead a high-performing team. Set clear goals, coach and develop people, give direct feedback, and build a culture of speed, ambition and ownership. At a Senior Manager level, set team objectives, coach and develop each person on the team.

  • Lead with AI. Build AI and agentic workflows into how the team spots stories, plans campaigns, pitches media and reports results, so the team works faster and smarter.

What you bring

  • A track record of viral campaigns. You have created campaigns that broke through nationally and drove measurable spikes in public attention, online and offline. You think in moments, images and headlines, and you move from idea to execution in hours, not weeks.

  • Fast paced. You are skilled in fast and excellent execution with rapid pivots and changing contexts.

  • A strong network. You have trusted relationships with German journalists, editors and producers (ideally including key decision makers), and connections in politics and civil society across the whole democratic political spectrum, including conservative circles. You can use your contacts to place stories.

  • Management. You have led and developed a team, or have mentored others and are ready to step into leading one. You set priorities, give direct feedback and bring out the best in people. At a Senior Manager level, you would move resources as the news and priorities shift.

  • Leadership presence. You are confident, credible and calm under pressure. You are an experienced, media-trained spokesperson on live TV and radio and in front of senior stakeholders, and you handle tough interviews, crisis moments and politically sensitive questions with ease.

  • AI First: You use AI tools every day and have built or improved workflows and automations with them. You know where AI adds speed and quality and where human judgement matters most, and you bring your team along.

Target experience

  • 5-8+ years in communications, campaigning, political communications, a newsroom or an agency.

  • 3+ years leading people, at Senior Manager level. We're also open to candidates at Manager level who have experience mentoring others and the ambition to lead a team.

  • A proven track record of national campaigns in Germany that created significant public attention and media coverage.

  • Experience as an organisation's spokesperson in national broadcast and / or print media.

  • Hands-on experience using AI in communications or campaigning work.

  • Native-level German (C2) and professional English.

Interested? Great! Here's what you should know

This role is based in Berlin. It is a full-time hybrid role, and we expect you to be in the Berlin office 2-3 days per week, with flexibility to work remotely for the rest of the week.

Our compensation philosophy is based on pay equity. All of our salaries are determined before we launch a role, based on a predetermined salary scale, the level on that scale and the cost of labour for that location. The annual salary for this role at Senior Manager level is €95,500 in Berlin. We are also open to candidates at the Manager level and the annual salary in Berlin is €83,500.

We recognise that people assess their qualifications differently, and you may not meet every requirement listed. If you believe you could be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply. Change.org is an open platform designed to serve people across the full range of viewpoints. Effectively supporting that mission requires teams with a wide variety of experiences, skills and perspectives, which we consider essential to our work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, age, or any other status protected by law.

We're committed to protecting your data. To learn more, please review our Change.org Job Applicant Privacy Policy.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout our recruitment process. If you need assistance or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know.

Professional-level English proficiency is required for all roles. While we are a global company, we ask that all CVs and application responses be submitted in English.

title: (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte (w/m/d) bei Dezernat Zukunft – Institut für Makrofinanzen
description:
Wer wir sind und was wir suchen

Ob die Energiewende gelingt, entscheidet sich nicht allein an Technologien, sondern an Kosten, Märkten und politischen Weichenstellungen. Genau dazu arbeitet das Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft – und um unsere Arbeit weiter zu vertiefen, suchen wir Dich. 

Das Dezernat Zukunft ist ein überparteilicher Berliner Think Tank an der Schnittstelle von Politik, Verwaltung und Forschung. Rund 30 Personen verfolgen gemeinsam das Ziel, Geld-, Finanz- und Wirtschaftspolitik neu zu denken und verständlich zu vermitteln. Geleitet von den Werten Würde, Wohlstand, Demokratie und Nachhaltigkeit suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt – idealerweise ab dem 1. Januar – für unser Energy Lab eine Person als (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte. 

In dieser Position konzipierst Du Analysen und Studien zu Energiemärkten – insbesondere zum Strommarkt – und führst sie eigenständig durch. Dabei betrachtest Du Energiekosten, Investitionsbedarfe, Gesamtsystemkosten sowie die Wechselwirkungen politischer Instrumente mit diesen Größen. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Fragen, wie sich Energiepolitik mit Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Nachhaltigkeit und Bezahlbarkeit zusammendenken lässt, wie Energiekosten strategisch und gezielt gesenkt werden können, und wie das regulatorische Umfeld so ausgestaltet werden kann, dass es den Erfolg der „zweiten Hälfte der Energiewende“ und damit die Erreichung der Klimaneutralität ermöglicht.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du analysierst Energiemärkte und -preise, einschließlich Systemkosten, und koordinierst dazu Forschungsprojekte. Dabei betrachtest Du auch fiskalpolitische Auswirkungen sowie Wechselwirkungen mit dem Stromnetzausbau. 
  • Du entwickelst konkrete Politikvorschläge, Analysen und Positionen zu den oben genannten Themen, in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Deinen Kolleg:innen im Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft sowie den weiteren Teams der Organisation. Außerdem organisierst Du Expert:innen-Gespräche und andere inhaltliche Veranstaltungen. 
  • Du interagierst aktiv mit Vertreter:innen von Parlamenten, Regierungen, Wissenschaft, Wirtschaft und Medien. Unsere Arbeit funktioniert nur dann, wenn wir mit diesen Gruppen im Austausch stehen, zuhören und zusammenarbeiten.

  • Aktive Unterstützung bei Deiner Weiterentwicklung – fachlich sowie in Bezug auf Kompetenzen, Netzwerke und Aufgaben. 
  • Einen Arbeitsplatz in Berlin-Mitte mit der Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten und gemeinsam vereinbarten Kernzeiten.
  • Unbürokratische, verständnisvolle Regelungen bei kurzfristigen Care-Bedarfen; bezahlte Freistellung nach § 29 TVöD bei persönlichen Anlässen (z. B. kranke Kinder). 
  • Einen Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket oder JobRad. 
  • Und nicht zuletzt: Ein dynamisches,motiviertes Team, gemeinsame Events (z. B. Berg- oder Paddel-Ausflüge) und Arbeit, die zählt. 


Dein Profil

  • Du teilst unsere Werte und Ziele, begeisterst Dich für Energie- und Klimapolitik und brennst dafür, dass die Transformation gelingt. 
  • Du hast einen Master-Abschluss in einem relevanten Fachgebiet sowie mindestens zwei Jahre einschlägige Berufserfahrung. Du kennst Dich in Energiemärkten – insbesondere im Strommarkt – aus, verstehst politische Instrumente und erkennst, welche Zahlen für politische Entscheidungen und ökonomische Weichenstellungen wirklich zählen. 
  • Du konzipierst und erstellst eigene Analysen – quantitativ wie textlich – selbstständig und gründlich. Du hast bereits erfolgreich Forschungsprojekte umgesetzt und Ergebnisse sowie politische Handlungsempfehlungen prägnant kommuniziert. Du bist Dir bewusst, dass unsere Analysen und Vorschläge in der Öffentlichkeit intensiv geprüft werden, und arbeitest entsprechend gewissenhaft und bist bereit, als Eigentümer:in für Deine Projekte einzustehen.
  • Du kommunizierst sehr gut in deutscher und englischer Sprache und verfasst in beiden Sprachen anspruchsvolle, gut verständliche Texte.
  • Du hast fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse in der praktischen Anwendung gängiger KI-Programme. 
  • Du willst den Dingen auf den Grund gehen und jeden Tag dazulernen. Noch wichtiger als mitgebrachtes Wissen ist für uns die Fähigkeit, es zu erweitern und Meinungen zu ändern. 
  • Du arbeitest gern im Team, hörst zu und unterstützt und förderst Deine Kolleg:innen.
Die perfekte Kandidat:in erfüllt nicht immer jede Anforderung. Wenn Du glaubst, dass Du zu uns passt – bewirb Dich gern trotzdem und sag uns, warum.


Beschäftigungsbeginn & Vertragsbedingungen

  • Beginn: Von uns aus so schnell wie möglich. Im Anschluss an das Bewerbungsverfahren rechnen wir mit einem Start im Januar 2027. Das genaue Startdatum ist verhandelbar.
