title: Manager: Compliance Advisory (and Data Protection)
description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and produt. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them , keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow.

The opportunity

We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products, not bolted at the end.

As our hands on compliance adviser in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

Compliance advisory is the heart of this role and will take around 70% of your time. You’ll also pick up a smaller, complementary slice of work as our Data Protection Officer (DPO), around 30% of your time. DPO experience is a plus but not essential, and we’ll train you if you need it.

What success looks like

In your first year, compliance advisory is where you’ve made your mark. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. You’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

Alongside that, in the smaller DPO part of your role, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand.

To do this you'll be involved in:

Compliance advisory (around 70% of your time)

  • Product development: turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start.

  • Product lifecycle management: keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures.

  • Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.

  • Marketing: working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged.

  • Service (Operations): building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use.

  • Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.

  • Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.

  • Working with second line (Protect): bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge.

Data Protection Officer (around 30% of your time - training will be provided if needed)

Being our DPO means:

  • advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs)

  • monitoring how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other global data protection laws and our own policies

  • training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection

  • being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data

As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data.

We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

We need a proactive compliance doer first and foremost. You get stuck in without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable tackling regulations you haven’t met before. You use your experience and expertise to help our teams find simple, clear and compliant solutions. Your advice is balanced, easy to follow and focused on the risks that matter most. You want to push the business forward, and you see good compliance as part of how we get there.

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

  • Compliance experience in the first (preferred) or second line of a UK regulated firm, ideally a bank, e-money institution or payments firm.

  • Practical knowledge of the rules behind our products, like Consumer Duty, BCOBS, CASS, FISMA, the Payment Services Regulations and the Money Laundering Regulations. As well as familiarity with HMRC requirements like BBSI and AEOI reporting.

  • Hands-on experience turning regulation into practical requirements for product, sales or operations teams.

  • An openness to picking up data protection as part of the role: a genuine interest is enough, DPO experience isn’t required.

  • A curious, questioning approach. You know the right questions to ask before signing something off, not just the rules to check it against.

  • The confidence to challenge, clearly and kindly, when something isn’t right.

  • A love of writing. We have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write).

Ideally, you would also:

  • Have deep expertise in at least one specialist area, such as payments, cards, Consumer Duty, BCOBS, financial promotions or similar.

  • Have been a DPO, or worked closely with one, in a regulated firm.

  • Have worked in finance or banking.

What can we offer you?

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

  • Salary: £ 80-90 (DOE)

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year)

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks

How long will the process take?

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

  • Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.

  • Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.

  • Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin.

  • Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview.

  • Step 5: Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here.

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We’re remote-first

We trust people to do great work wherever they are. We hire across the UK and most of our team works remotely full-time. We have a small London office in Moorgate for those who want it, and about a third of the company is close enough to use it occasionally, but there's no expectation to be there. What matters is the work, not where you do it.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
At Deliverect, our API-first platform is revolutionizing commerce by providing a connected suite of on and off-premise solutions. We empower both the food and retail industries to expand their revenue and simplify their operations, creating seamless experiences for businesses to sell anywhere and deliver everywhere. Join us in this exciting journey, where your contributions will directly impact how businesses connect with their customers in a rapidly evolving global market.

Department Focus

The Product Department at Deliverect is at the forefront of the digital ordering revolution, dedicated to consistently delivering groundbreaking solutions to the global marketplace. Our team of passionate and innovative engineers, designers, and product managers architect tools that empower businesses to thrive in the evolving digital landscape, streamlining digital ordering for delivery and on-premise services. We are committed to creating user-friendly, dependable, and scalable technology that simplifies operations and enhances customer experiences, playing an integral role in the success of businesses worldwide. In our department, innovation is not just a concept; it's the driving force behind everything we do.

Your Impact

As a Senior Product Manager at Deliverect, you will own the end-to-end lifecycle of critical product initiatives, as well as be a driving force behind Deliverect's expansion into new markets, working hand in hand with our GTM teams to determine what it takes to win in each one — and then making sure we build and deliver it. In addition, you will be leveraging Product-Led Growth (PLG) strategies to drive self-serve adoption of features and user retention. Your ability to balance technical complexity with a customer-centric approach will directly impact company revenue, operational efficiency, and customer satisfaction across the global marketplace.


This is a full-time, hybrid role with a flexible work schedule, offering 3 days in our Paris offfice and 2 days from the comfort of your home.


What you will do
  • Unlock New Markets Alongside GTM: Act as the product counterpart to our GTM teams on market expansion. You will run detailed assessments of each target market to pinpoint the capability gaps and opportunities that decide whether we win there — local POS and delivery-platform integrations, payment methods, localization, and regulatory or fiscal requirements — and translate those findings into clearly specified, prioritized product requirements with a defensible case for sequencing.

  • Lead Product Strategy & Roadmap Development: Own the end-to-end product lifecycle from ideation to launch, developing detailed business cases and roadmaps aligned with Deliverect's growth objectives.

  • Own Successful Market Rollout: Partner closely with GTM, Sales, and Onboarding to make sure each new-market launch actually lands. You will define launch readiness criteria, equip commercial and implementation teams with what they need to sell and deploy the product locally, and close the loop on early market feedback so that the second and third customers in a market are meaningfully easier to win than the first.

  • Drive Product Led Growth (PLG) Initiatives: Architect and optimize self-serve onboarding funnels, in-product upgrade paths, and usage-driven tier models to drive user expansion and maximize platform value.

  • Cross-Functional Execution & Technical Collaboration: Partner closely with engineering, architecture, and design teams to build scalable solutions, including managing technical requirements for APIs and core platform integrations.

  • Stakeholder Management & Alignment: Act as a primary communicator to present clear product updates, pitch business cases, and influence alignment across all internal departments and external partners.

  • Data, Market & Competitive Analysis: Define and track product KPIs, and continuously leverage analytics, competitive intelligence, and customer insights — at both product and individual market level — to prioritize the backlog and resolve complex user friction points.

    • What you will Bring
  • Product Management Expertise: 5+ years of experience managing SaaS products within an agile environment, preferably in the food tech, SaaS, foodservice, or hospitality sectors.

  • Market Expansion Experience: A track record of taking a product into new geographies or segments — assessing local requirements, competitive gaps, and compliance needs, then shipping the changes required to compete there. Direct experience with localization, regional integrations, or multi-market rollouts is a strong advantage.

  • PLG Growth Mindset: Proven experience developing and optimizing self-serve user funnels, upgrade paths, or usage-driven monetization tiers.

  • Domain Knowledge: Deep familiarity with campaign management systems, online ordering networks, POS integrations, or technical API-first software architectures.

  • Data-Driven & Analytical Skills: Strong track record of tracking product KPIs, building data-backed business cases, and making high-impact prioritization decisions.

  • Collaborative Leadership: Demonstrated success leading cross-functional squads and complex projects through influence, clear communication, and empathetic stakeholder negotiation — including working effectively with commercial and regional teams across time zones.

  • Education: A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Business, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
    • Join Our Innovative Journey:

    At Deliverect, we're not just building a platform; we're redefining how restaurants and retailers connect with their customers globally. We're looking for agile, ambitious, and resourceful team members who are excited to tackle complex challenges, take calculated risks and contribute to innovative solutions that shape the future of commerce.

    What You'll Gain by Joining Us:

    Invest in Your Growth- We provide a dedicated learning budget to help you expand your skills and knowledge in this dynamic environment.
    Solve Meaningful Challenges- Contribute to tackling some of the most significant challenges in the global tech industry, directly impacting the way businesses operate worldwide.
    Drive Innovation- Immerse yourself in a culture where innovation isn't just a buzzword – our weekly releases and new features ensure you're always working on cutting-edge solutions.
    Collaborate with a Global Team- Be part of a diverse, international team that values transparency, visibility, and a multitude of perspectives.
    Be Part of a Unicorn- Join a rapidly scaling SaaS unicorn at the forefront of the order management industry, where your contributions have significant impact.
    Enjoy Regionally Tailored Rewards- Our compensation and benefits packages are thoughtfully designed to reflect the unique needs of each market, ensuring you’re supported with what matters most—right where you are.

    We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and has equal opportunities to succeed. We strongly encourage applications from underrepresented groups.

● Structured thinking – analytical, well organized and confident in Excel and PowerPoint (old school, we know, but we use it and need it)

What We Offer

title: Visiting Analyst - Investment Team (m/f/d)
description:
About Planet A

Planet A is a leading early-stage European tech VC backing founders tackling the world’s greatest systemic challenges. We take a scientific approach to identify breakthrough solutions the world can’t afford to ignore across energy, resource mastery, neo-manufacturing, and critical infrastructure. Investments include Aris Machina, Staer, INERATEC, Gigaton and Makersite.

  • Employment: Full-time internship (40 hours/week)

  • Duration: 6 months

  • Location: Remote within the EU (Preference to Berlin, London, Munich, Zurich and Stockholm)

  • Start Date: As soon as possible

Tasks

You’ll work directly with one of our Partners on the most important thing a VC does: finding exceptional founders before everyone else does. This is a hands-on sourcing seat, not a back-office position.

  • Find exceptional founders early. Identify promising founders, spinouts and research teams through LinkedIn, GitHub, scientific papers, patents, university labs and relevant communities.

  • Build a sourcing engine. Develop and run your own sourcing playbooks, using AI and automation to identify promising opportunities at a scale that manual research cannot match.

  • Screen inbound deal flow. Quickly assess incoming opportunities and flag the most promising cases to the investment team.

  • Maintain our CRM. Keep our CRM accurate and up to date, ensuring leads, interactions and relationships are properly tracked.

  • Build tools, not just workflows. Work with our Data / Engineering team to turn successful sourcing approaches into repeatable tools and systems.

Requirements

  • Highly analytical. You form clear views from data, evidence and first principles.

  • AI-native. You actively use AI tools and agents, experiment with new approaches and constantly look for ways to automate work.

title: Founder & CEO (Vico Lead) mit SAP-Fokus
description:

(Offices: Berlin, Frankfurt, Barcelona, Seville)

Vicoland gives the professional services market a new dimension: Virtual Companies - “Vicos”. We invented Vicos as a new type of supplier, more efficient than traditional professional services firms (consultancies, system integrators, agencies etc.). We have received 20 million € in round A financing.

Vicos may consist of freelancers, SMEs and AI agents. Vicos have proven to be more cost-efficient and to deliver better quality than traditional companies.

Therefore, we look for proven leaders in SAP services to become successful Vico Leads with our backing and support. Thereby, you grow your Vico beyond 10M+ € in revenue and 6-7-digit personal income.

Some great leaders in SAP consulting have the ambition to become entrepreneurs. Few, however, act on it because the classic way to start a business is expensive and risky. Vícoland gives you the opportunity to (a) avoid the expenses and risk and (b) offer clients the unique benefits of services delivered by Vicos.

Your opportunity: cross the €10 million € revenue line within two years

We are looking for founders who want to take their Vico to €10 million in revenue and more, within about two years. Vicos can grow to multi-million € revenue already within 12 months.

• Your business: Your clients, your offer, your positioning. You decide what you build and how fast you grow.

• Your team: You build your team from freelancers and SMEs and can bind key people to your Vico by contract.

• Your profit & asset: Your Vico's profit is yours. You or a personal company of yours is general contractor of the Vico. Which means you can also sell the business you build as your Vico.

What Vicoland offers

We provide extensive support and backing to enable and accelerate your business building:

• Infrastructure: Our certified platform covers marketing, finance, legal and organization, so you can run your Vico end-to-end without overhead.

• Market access: You can use Vicoland GmbH’s listing with major corporations to make business with them immediately.

• Sales support: We provide leads from our enterprise pipeline and support in acquisition.

• Sourcing: You get access to thousands of experts, with a strong focus on SAP, and support in finding the right people for your team anywhere in the world.

• Financial services: We provide insurance and factoring.

• Mentoring: You get guidance from experienced Vicoland professionals.

• Transition: If you are moving from employment, we give you financial security for the transition.

You run your Vico as its founder & CEO, that is Vico Lead. You:

• Win clients from your own network and build your own pipeline. Leads from Vicoland add to it, they do not replace it.

• Pitch, close deals and grow your client relationships.

title: AI Ops Engineer (Business Operations)
description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 10x YoY.

The Role

We’re looking for an AI Ops Engineer to build the internal systems that help Kernel scale without adding unnecessary manual work. You’ll work across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations - finding the highest-leverage problems and building practical AI-powered workflows.

This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll take ideas from a vague business problem to a tool or workflow that people use, then maintain and improve it in production. You’ll choose the fastest sensible approach for each problem - coding agents, automation platforms, APIs, data pipelines or lightweight code.

You’ll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations, and partner closely with GTM, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define how an AI-native company operates: help build Kernel’s internal playbook for using AI across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations

  • Make our GTM team more productive: automate the repetitive work in prospecting, account research, meeting prep and CRM hygiene, so BDRs, AEs and Account Managers spend more time with customers

  • Build internal tools and workflows: use coding agents, APIs, automation platforms, no-code tools or lightweight code

  • Turn company data into operational leverage: connect and improve data across our systems, then put it to work in AI agents, proactive workflows and better decision-making

  • Put AI agents to work across Kernel: give teams agents with the right context, tools and guardrails so they can move faster without sacrificing judgement or reliability

  • Be Kernel’s own internal customer: deploy Kernel on Kernel’s CRM, improve our GTM data and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering

  • Level up the team: help colleagues become confident AI users, document what works and turn successful experiments into repeatable ways of working

Your First 6 Months

For your first six months, you’ll focus on our sales team. You’ll sit with our BDRs, AEs and Account Managers and learn how they work day to day. Then you’ll automate everything that doesn’t need a human. That means going deep on Salesforce and our GTM stack, and owning the RevOps workflows behind them. After that, you’ll bring the same approach to Marketing, Customer Success and Operations.

What You Bring

  • A track record of shipping: you’ve built tools, automations or AI workflows that people use every day, ideally inside a small, fast-moving startup. Around 2–5 years of experience is typical, but what you’ve built matters more than your years. Ex-founders welcome

  • Experience inside a high-growth startup, or building your own, is highly desirable

  • Curious about sales: you’re keen to learn how our BDRs and AEs work, and how Salesforce is set up, before you build for them

  • AI-tool obsessed: you are constantly testing new models, agents, MCPs and workflows, and you have the judgement to turn them into reliable systems that people actually adopt

  • Strong data instincts: you can turn fragmented, messy information into reliable workflows and create feedback loops that keep it trustworthy

  • Can’t unsee inefficiency: you see the company as a connected system; when you find a broken or unnecessarily manual process, your instinct is to understand it, build the fix and make sure it sticks

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

  • Prefer deep specialization over breadth: this role means switching between projects and teams, depending on business needs

  • Prefer steady-state work over project-based sprints: priorities will shift as the business evolves

  • Only want “strategic” work: you will personally build the tools, clean the data and fix the workflows

❌ This role is definitely not for you if you:

  • Need every task to be clearly scoped before starting: ambiguity and learning on the fly are constant

  • Avoid operational grunt work or lose interest after the prototype

  • Want to protect a 9-to-6 or a mostly remote setup: we are in the office together 4–5 days a week and the pace is high

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. The machine that builds the product

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.

I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.

That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.

Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.

You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.

What you'll do

Build the machine that builds the product

Most of your time goes here.

  • Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

  • Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

  • Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.

Own the platform

  • Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

  • Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

  • Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.

Work across the stack

  • Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

  • Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

  • Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.

Your first six months

  • Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

  • At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

  • Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

  • Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.

How you'll work

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.

You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.

This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.

You'll probably enjoy this if

  • You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one.

  • You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it.

  • You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week.

  • You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so.

  • Infrastructure as code as a habit, with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code.

TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.

description:
INTERNSHIP 

Agentic AI for Semi-Automating the Data Science Workflow 

Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. 

Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models. 

Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices. 

Key Figures 

  • 20 years of experience in data science 

  • 500+ data scientists, all consultants 

  • 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 

  • 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) 

  • $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 

  • 1,000+ data science projects 

Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. 

A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. 

Internship Objective: From a Business Question to a Trusted Recommendation 

LLM-based agents have made rapid progress in the past two years: they can now write, run and tune machine learning code with little human help. Yet real data science projects rarely start from a clean, well-defined task. They start from a business question and imperfect data, and the early choices (what to predict, how to measure success, how to validate) decide whether the result can be trusted. Automating these steps calls for assistants that know when to ask, when to stop, and how to back every claim with evidence. 

The Innovation Department is building remit, a harness that semi-automates the data science workflow. At each step of a project (framing, data design, exploratory analysis, modeling, evaluation), AI agents draft the output, automatic checks catch common mistakes such as data leakage, and a data scientist reviews and accepts the result before moving on. Ultimately, a business user brings a question and a dataset, and the system frames the problem, prepares and explores the data, compares models against a simple baseline, and returns a clear recommendation in which every figure can be traced back to the data. 

The work builds on recent research in agentic data science [1]. Agents now earn medals on many of the Kaggle competitions in MLE-bench [2], yet they tend to guess silently rather than ask when a task is ambiguous [3]. Meanwhile, tabular foundation models such as TabICLv2 [4] give strong predictive models without any tuning. 

The intern will work with senior data scientists and AI builders to build and refine remit. This internship offers an opportunity to engage with cutting-edge AI research and production engineering. 

Key Responsibilities 

The intern will: 

  • Review the latest research on agentic data science and on the evaluation of AI agents, building on the team's recent review. 

  • Design and implement remit's agents, starting with problem framing and data design, together with the automatic checks that catch mistakes such as data leakage. 

  • Help define how the system works with business users: when to ask a clarifying question, when to stop rather than guess, and how to explain results in plain language. 

  • Extend the system toward modeling and evaluation, building on trusted tools (scikit-learn, AutoML, tabular foundation models) rather than free-form generated code. 

  • Build a benchmark of realistic business cases, run experiments to measure quality, reliability and cost, and take part in a pilot with business users. 

  • Help integrate the system with the Databricks stack (Unity Catalog, MLflow) and support the safe and governed operation of the agents. 

Profile 

  • Currently in the final year of a Master's or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming. 

  • Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research-and-build problem and to explain results to non-specialists. 

  • Familiarity with large language models and agentic techniques (prompting, tool calling, structured outputs, evaluation). 

  • Strong Python skills and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). 

  • Fluency in English. 

  • Nice to have: experience with an agent framework, solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing), and exposure to Databricks, MLflow or cloud data platforms. 

Benefits 

  • Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact. 

  • Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetrics' Innovation Department. 

  • Skill Development: Gain expertise in LLM agents, the evaluation of AI systems, and production tooling on Databricks (Unity Catalog, MLflow). 

  • Career Growth: Opportunity to transition into a full-time Data Scientist role in AI at Ekimetrics, or into a PhD program, upon successful completion of the internship. 

  • Scientific Contribution: Opportunity to co-author and publish scientific papers in reputable AI and data science conferences and journals. 

  • Networking: Collaborate with Ekimetrics' industrial and academic partners, enhancing your professional network in the AI research community. 

  • Ethical and Sustainable AI: Learn to develop AI solutions that align with ethical, governed, and sustainable best practices, a core commitment of Ekimetrics. 

Duration: 6 months, Paris

[1] LLM-Based Data Science Agents: A Survey of Capabilities, Challenges, and Future Directions (2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04023

description:
Latent Reasoning for Tabular Foundation Models: Performance Enhancement and Interpretability 

 

 

Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. 

Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models. 

Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices. 

Key Figures 

  • 20 years of experience in data science 

  • 500+ data scientists, all consultants 

  • 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 

  • 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) 

  • $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 

  • 1,000+ data science projects 

Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. 

A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. 

 

Internship Objective: From Latent Reasoning to Better and More Understandable Tabular Models 

 

Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) such as TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT are transformers pre-trained on large collections of mostly synthetic datasets. They learn in context: the training data and the points to predict are given as input, and predictions come out of a single forward pass, with no dataset-specific training or tuning. They now rival gradient boosting on many benchmarks [3], which is changing how tabular modeling is practiced. 

In large language models, a growing line of research lets the model “reason” in its latent space rather than through generated tokens, using extra depth-wise computation, reused continuous hidden states or internal iterations. This latent reasoning can improve performance without longer text outputs [1, 2]. Our hypothesis is that a similar mechanism can improve TFMs: spending more latent compute at inference on hard or ambiguous cases could help them make better use of the in-context examples. Almost all existing work on latent reasoning targets natural language, and its transfer to tabular models, whose architecture, pre-training data and output differ profoundly, remains largely unexplored. 

Mechanistic interpretability is starting to open the black box, both for latent-reasoning language models and for TFMs themselves [4]. It lets us ask not only whether latent reasoning improves a TFM, but also what the model actually computes during these extra steps, and whether that computation is faithful and useful. The internship therefore has two goals: designing and evaluating latent reasoning mechanisms for TFMs, and using interpretability methods to analyze what they learn. 

The intern will work with senior researchers and data scientists. This internship offers an opportunity to contribute to an emerging research topic at the intersection of tabular modeling, latent reasoning and interpretability. 

Key Responsibilities 

The intern will: 

  • Review the literature on latent reasoning (NLP) and tabular foundation models, building on recent surveys. 

  • Identify and adapt latent reasoning mechanisms to TFM architectures (e.g. iterative depth-wise computation, hidden-state reuse). 

  • Implement them on open-source TFMs and measure their effect on accuracy, calibration and robustness against strong baselines (gradient boosting, standard TFMs) at comparable compute. 

  • Apply interpretability methods (representation analysis, probing, activation patching) to characterize the computation performed during latent reasoning. 

  • Build an evaluation protocol on diverse tabular datasets, including realistic business cases. 

  • Document the results and contribute to scientific publications. 

Profile 

  • Currently in the final year of a Master’s or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming. 

  • Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines. 

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research problem. 

  • Knowledge of transformers and language models; familiarity with latent reasoning or recurrent-depth models is a plus. 

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills, and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). 

  • Fluency in English is a plus. 

  • Nice to have: experience in interpretability, knowledge of TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT, and solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing). 

Benefits 

  • Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact. 

  • Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetrics' Innovation Department. 

  • Skill Development: Gain expertise in LLM agents, the evaluation of AI systems, and production tooling on Databricks (Unity Catalog, MLflow). 

  • Career Growth: Opportunity to transition into a full-time Data Scientist role in AI at Ekimetrics, or into a PhD program, upon successful completion of the internship. 

  • Scientific Contribution: Opportunity to co-author and publish scientific papers in reputable AI and data science conferences and journals. 

  • Networking: Collaborate with Ekimetrics' industrial and academic partners, enhancing your professional network in the AI research community. 

  • Ethical and Sustainable AI: Learn to develop AI solutions that align with ethical, governed, and sustainable best practices, a core commitment of Ekimetrics. 

Duration: 6 months, Paris 

References

[2] Chen, X. et al. (2025). Reasoning Beyond Language: A Comprehensive Survey on Latent Chain-of-Thought Reasoning. arXiv:2505.16782. 

[3] Tabular Foundation Models: A Systematic Survey. [authors, year, link to complete]

About us

Role Summary

We're looking for a Product Manager to own the editor: the surface every Photoroom user touches, on iOS, Android and the web. You'll sit in our Product Foundations team, whose mission is to build the core experiences that power Photoroom. You will work on the last-mile editing problem, giving users control with fine-grained edits for photos and videos. Working closely with engineers, designers, and the PMs who depend on you, you'll decide what gets built, why, and how it ships.

Location: Paris, Ile de France (Hybrid)

About the role

  • Own the single- and multi-image editing experiences end to end. Build one unified visual editing experience across three platforms, iOS, Android, Web and API.

  • Integrate visual editing experiences within chat editing. Photoroom gives users the ability to start with AI generation and then graduate into fine-grained editing tasks. You’ll work hand-in-hand with our researchers and engineers to make sure our users can traverse the full editing journey in Photoroom.

  • Define the problem before the solution. Sharpen the user problem, then partner with design and engineering to ship work that feels effortless. On a surface this heavily used, the difference between "works" and "feels right" is the whole job.

  • Stay close to the user. Talk to e-commerce sellers every week, watch them edit, and feed what you hear directly into roadmap decisions.

  • Use data to decide, not to justify. Pull and interpret data yourself, including crash rates, latency and cross-platform parity, to form hypotheses, measure what shipped, and call what's next. You won't need to wait around for someone else to run the query.

About You

  • You've shipped products people love. Five+ years as a PM, with multiple launches where you’ve convincingly solved the user problem and delivered business value.

  • You've owned a creative product surface. An editor, a canvas or another tool where you are giving a user creative control.

  • AI has reshaped how you work. You use Claude or equivalent every day, for prototyping, testing with users, or automating the parts of the job that used to fill your calendar. The value you bring sits in strategy and direction, not in writing tickets.

  • You have demonstrable product taste. You can show specific work where the details matter and explain the calls you made, including the ones you'd make differently now. Craft in an editor is measured in milliseconds and pixels.

  • You create clarity from ambiguity. Given a fuzzy problem, you take action rather than waiting for direction: you structure it, decide what matters, and move.

  • You're data-fluent. You pull, interpret, and challenge data yourself, and use it to form a point of view rather than confirm one.

  • You thrive in small teams with high autonomy. You can ship without being managed, and can operate in a fully remote, async-first environment that offers no scaffolding around you.

Nice to have: experience building creative tools or any product where craft and visual quality matter; an understanding of photography or videography; experience shipping native mobile alongside web; entrepreneurial experience (you've started, built, or run something).

description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 5 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons notre futur(e) post-doctorant(e) en évaluation de la vulnérabilité d’un réseau d’accès Télécom de type PON (Passive Optical Network) vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS (Distributed Acoustic Sensor) pour rejoindre le département Communications et Electronique (COMELEC).

Cette étude se situe dans le cadre du projet « Ecoute Acoustique Terrestre » (EAT) RAPID (Régime d’Appui Pour l’Innovation Duale), fruit d’un partenariat entre la société Febus Optics et Télécom Paris.

 La mesure de vibrations acoustiques distribuées par fibre optique (DAS, Distributed Acoustic Sensing) est une technologie récente, dont les applications ne cessent de se diversifier. On peut citer par exemple la détection d’intrusion en surveillance périmétrique, les mesures sismiques, le diagnostic de puits (pétrole, géothermie), etc. La bande passante de la mesure, de sub-Hertz à la centaine de kiloHertz, permet également d’envisager la captation de la bande audio, et donc de réaliser des mesures audios sur une fibre optique. Il est ainsi possible d’utiliser le réseau optique télécom d’un bâtiment pour réaliser des écoutes, en utilisant un système DAS modifié, intégrant des artéfacts matériels particuliers (enroulement, antennes, connecteurs) au voisinage de la zone d’écoute et un traitement du signal spécifique pour obtenir des performances suffisantes.

Le cadre de ce Postdoc est d’évaluer la vulnérabilité d’un réseau télécom vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS. Le branchement sur un réseau optique Telecom local en fonctionnement nécessite de s’adapter à son architecture, notamment en termes de plan de longueur d’onde.

L’audit des systèmes de télécommunication afin d’en évaluer la vulnérabilité constitue un enjeu majeur du réseau télécom. Un exemple de configuration d’un réseau d’accès est décrit dans la figure ci-après. Depuis le réseau Backbone, à partir du ‘Central Office’, les signaux télécoms sont acheminés chez les abonnés via le PON (Passive Optical Network). À l’intérieur des bâtiments, un réseau FTTX (Fiber To The X=H home, X=R room, X=O office, etc) ou un réseau local LAN (Local Area Network) optique servent respectivement à acheminer le signal optique jusqu’au terminal final ou à communiquer entre deux terminaux locaux via une liaison optique. Le PON comprend une fibre nourricière (Feeder Fiber) puis, au moins, un coupleur 1×N. Le codage de l’information est alors un mélange de multiplexage en longueur d’onde grossier (C-WDM) et de multiplexage temporel (TDM). Chaque voie de sortie du coupleur 1×N est envoyée vers des groupes de 1 à n abonnés à travers, au moins, un filtre qui sélectionne la longueur d’onde qui leur est allouée. Le signal après ce filtre est alors monochromatique et codé TDM. Le dernier coupleur 1×n répartie le signal chez les n abonnés. Ce PON comprend donc, entre autres, des coupleurs passifs qui divisent les signaux vers différents abonnés mais aussi des connecteurs, soudures, etc.

L’objectif de ce Postdoc est de faire un état des lieux des différents types de réseau mis en place et d’en évaluer les conséquences sur la capacité de mesures DAS :

·         Description des différents types de réseaux locaux existants,

·         Etats des lieux des différents types de transmission : CWDM, TDM, …

·         Quels sont les différents points d’accès pour une mesure DAS ?

·         Comment discriminer les différentes fibres interrogées après un coupleur ? Influence des points réflecteurs,

·         Etude des différentes marges de puissance pour une mesure DAS,

·         Potentielle présence de nœuds d’insertion et limite de la transparence optique,

·         Sensibilité des mesures DAS en fonction des différents types de fibre et de leur environnement,

·         Influence du réflecteur final sur la capacité d’écoute.

Le caractère innovant sera la définition des conditions du réseau et des configurations et des performances DAS permettant un audit cyber sur des infrastructures déjà déployées.

Au-delà d’une synthèse des configurations que l’on peut trouver sur le terrain, il s’agira de mener des tests, soit sur un réseau réel auxquels un accès nous sera donné, soit sur un réseau modèle implémenté pour l’étude. Ces travaux permettront d’identifier le type de modules d’interfaçage nécessaires, et de les spécifier, puis de les concevoir et de les fabriquer.

Vos principales missions seront :

  • Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine des capteurs à fibre optique distribués

  • Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

  • Participer à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris


Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat en génie électrique, en communications optiques, en photonique, en capteurs optiques ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez d’une solide expertise théorique et pratique en photonique et en traitement du signal numérique, ainsi que de bonnes compétences en programmation. Une connaissance des algorithmes de traitement du signal appliqués aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique, notamment dans le cadre de la détection cohérente, constitue un atout. You keep Alpha's cost and schedule baselines honest against each other. Without a credible risk register and change process, changes slip into the program outside any controlled path, the IMS and cost forecast quietly drift apart, and a gate review surprises leadership with numbers nobody signed off on. Your job is to prevent that by making risk and change management a live, trusted function from the earliest stage of delivery, rather than something bolted on once problems have compounded.

  • Able to build a risk and change framework from scratch, not just administer an inherited one; you know what good governance looks like before it exists

  • Confident holding the line on change discipline with internal engineers and external partners who have their own priorities, combining analytical rigor with the communication skills to make it stick

  • Comfortable working with high autonomy while program structure is still being built

  • Fluent in English; German is a strong advantage given the contractor and regulatory landscape

  • Familiar with AI tools and digital ways of working, and quick to adapt in a lean, fast-paced environment

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. als Senior Accounting Manager DACH (m/w/d)

LAKRIDS BY BÜLOW wurde 2007 von Johan Bülow in Dänemark gegründet und ist eine der einzigartigsten Marken Skandinaviens.

Alle Gourmet Lakritz Spezialitäten kommen aus unserer eigenen Produktion in Dänemark, werden aus natürlichen Zutaten hergestellt, und sind heute sowohl in unseren eigenen Retail Stores als auch in den besten Food-, Design- und Concept Stores weltweit erhältlich.

Wir bei LAKRIDS BY BÜLOW sind ein großartiges, herzliches und internationales Team mit einem gemeinsamen Ziel: WE MAKE THE WORLD LOVE LIQUORICE.

Deine Aufgaben:

• Gesamtverantwortung: Du verantwortest das Rechnungswesen der Gesellschaften in Deutschland und Österreich und setzt es operativ um – ordnungsgemäß nach HGB, GoBD und Steuerrecht.

• Organisation & Dienstleister: Du steuerst externe Partner (Steuerberatung, Payroll), legst Zuständigkeiten und Freigaberegelungen fest und baust das Accounting für den geplanten Markteintritt in der Schweiz auf.

• Monats- & Jahresabschluss: Du erstellst Monats- und Jahresabschlüsse, den HGB-Jahresabschluss gemeinsam mit der Steuerberatung, führst das Hauptbuch inkl. Abstimmung der Bilanzkonten, verantwortest Abgrenzungen, Rückstellungen und Anlagenbuchhaltung und koordinierst die Abschlussprüfung.

• Laufende Buchhaltung & Liquidität: Du verantwortest Debitoren und Kreditoren inkl. Spesen, Forderungsmanagement und Mahnwesen, gibst Zahlungsläufe im Vier-Augen-Prinzip frei und steuerst Liquiditätsplanung und tägliche Bankabstimmung.

• Steuern & Compliance: Du kümmerst dich um Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldungen und ZM (ggf. OSS), betriebliche Steuererklärungen mit der Steuerberatung, Betriebsprüfungen und Kassennachschauen, Kassen-Compliance (KassenSichV/TSE, RKSV) und statistische Meldungen (z. B. Intrastat). Für Österreich verantwortest du den UGB-Jahresabschluss mit der lokalen Steuerberatung inkl. Offenlegung.

• Konzern & Intercompany: Du lieferst monatliche Reporting-Packages an Group Finance, stimmst Intercompany-Salden und -Verrechnungen ab und unterstützt bei Verrechnungspreisdokumentation, Budget und Forecast.

• Retail Finance & Filialen: Du stimmst Filialumsätze (POS), Bargeld- und Kartenzahlungen ab, begleitest Warenbewegungen und Inventuren, Gutscheine und Geschenkkarten sowie Filialmieten, Nebenkosten und Mietkautionen und analysierst die Filialergebnisse.

• Internes Kontrollsystem & Prozesse: Du baust das IKS auf (u. a. Vier-Augen-Prinzip, Funktionstrennung), treibst die Digitalisierung von Prozessen und Systemen voran und erstellst Bilanzierungs- und Prozessrichtlinien.

Dein Profil

• Abgeschlossenes Studium mit Schwerpunkt Rechnungswesen/Finance oder kaufmännische Ausbildung mit Weiterbildung zur:zum Bilanzbuchhalter:in

• Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Rechnungswesen, davon idealerweise einige Jahre in verantwortlicher Rolle

• Sicherer Umgang mit HGB, GoBD und deutschem Steuerrecht; Kenntnisse in UGB und österreichischem Steuerrecht sind ein Plus

• Erfahrung im Filial- bzw. Retailgeschäft (POS, Kasse, Inventuren) und mit Kassen-Compliance

• Erfahrung im Reporting an eine internationale Muttergesellschaft und mit Intercompany-Themen

• Routine in der Zusammenarbeit mit Steuerberatung und Wirtschaftsprüfung

• Erfahrung mit Payroll (DE/AT) ist ein Plus

• Hands-on-Mentalität, Struktur und Lust, Prozesse und ein IKS aufzubauen

• Affinität für digitale Tools und ERP-Systeme [ e.g. Navision]

• Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse

Was wir bieten

• Eine Schlüsselrolle mit echtem Gestaltungsspielraum: Du baust Strukturen, Prozesse und das IKS mit auf

• Die Chance, weitere Expansionen zu begleiten

• Bei Interesse und passender Erfahrung kannst du perspektivisch auch die Payroll-Schnittstelle übernehmen

• Kurze Entscheidungswege und enge Zusammenarbeit mit Geschäftsführung und Group Finance in Kopenhagen

• Ein internationales Umfeld mit einer Premiummarke

• Personalrabatt auf unsere Produkte

Klingt das nach dir ?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung mit Lebenslauf, Gehaltsvorstellung und frühestmöglichem Eintrittstermin.

Inclusion & Diversity commitment

Bei LAKRIDS BY BÜLOW setzen wir uns dafür ein, einen vielfältigen, gleichberechtigten und inklusiven Arbeitsplatz in allen Märkten und Funktionsbereichen zu fördern. Wir sind davon überzeugt, dass vielfältige Perspektiven unsere Teams und unsere Ergebnisse stärken.

description:
Über Simplyright

Wir bei Simplyright helfen unseren Kunden dabei, ihr Recht schnell und unkompliziert durchzusetzen. Unser Fokus liegt unter anderem darauf, unzulässige Kontogebühren von Banken zurückzufordern oder zu viel gezahlte Beiträge während des Lockdowns von Fitnessstudios zurückzuholen. In unserem Team mit 11 bis 50 Mitarbeitenden arbeiten wir gemeinsam daran, juristische Prozesse für Verbraucher zugänglich zu machen.

Deine Aufgaben im Backoffice

  • Du bearbeitest Kundenanliegen und administrative Vorgänge im Innendienst.

  • Du pflegst und verwaltest Kundenakten im System.

  • Du stehst im telefonischen Austausch mit Mandanten und betreust sie bei Fragen zu ihren Verfahren.

  • Du korrespondierst schriftlich über unser Ticketsystem mit Kunden.

Das bringst du mit

Für diese unbefristete Vollzeitstelle mit 40 Wochenstunden bringst du Organisationstalent und Zuverlässigkeit im administrativen Bereich mit. Wenn du dich in den Aufgaben wiederfindest und nicht jede einzelne Anforderung zu hundert Prozent erfüllst, freuen wir uns trotzdem über deine Bewerbung.

Deine ersten Monate bei Simplyright

In den ersten Monaten wirst du dich intensiv in unsere Abläufe im Backoffice einarbeiten, Kundenakten eigenständig bearbeiten und den direkten Kontakt zu unseren Mandanten übernehmen. Du lernst unsere internen Systeme kennen und unterstützt das Team tatkräftig bei der Durchsetzung von Kundenansprüchen.

Wichtig – Arbeitsmittel: Ein Windows-Laptop oder Windows-PC sowie ein Headset werden nicht vom Arbeitgeber gestellt. Du bringst beides selbst mit und nutzt es für deine Arbeit.

Vergütung und Benefits

Für diese Position bieten wir ein Gehalt im Rahmen von EUR 2,500–2,800 per month. Du profitierst von flexiblem Homeoffice und kannst komplett remote arbeiten. Zudem unterstützen wir dich mit bezahlten Krankheitstagen und zusätzlichen Urlaubstagen.

title: (Senior) GEO Manager (m/w/d)
description:
At idealo, we've built a strong SEO foundation. Now, we're looking to take the next step. As AI-powered search experiences such as ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Gemini increasingly influence how people research products and make purchasing decisions, we want to ensure idealo becomes a trusted and frequently cited source within these new shopping journeys.

As our GEO Manager, you'll take ownership of developing Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) as an additional growth discipline alongside our established SEO activities. Combining your technical SEO expertise with hands-on experience in AI search optimization, you'll develop our GEO strategy, establish meaningful visibility monitoring, and drive experimentation to understand what makes content and data discoverable, relevant, and citable by generative AI systems.

You'll work closely with our SEO team and collaborate across Product, Engineering, Content, Brand, and Communications to turn emerging opportunities into scalable solutions.

About your new role

  • GEO Strategy & Development: You develop and drive idealo's GEO strategy and experimentation roadmap, building on our existing SEO foundation. You identify opportunities across generative search platforms and AI-assisted shopping journeys, translating emerging developments into actionable initiatives aligned with our broader SEO and business objectives.

  • AI Visibility & Performance Monitoring: You establish and continuously improve a GEO monitoring framework covering platforms such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews. You define relevant KPIs, including mention and citation rates, share of voice, sentiment, and positioning within AI-generated answers, and develop dashboards that make performance and progress transparent to different stakeholders.

  • Technical GEO Optimization: You leverage your technical SEO expertise to improve how generative AI systems discover, interpret, and reference idealo's content. This includes optimizing structured data (Schema.org), semantic relationships, product and offer information, and identifying technical opportunities to strengthen our visibility and accessibility across AI-powered search experiences.

  • Experimentation & Competitive Analysis: You design, implement, and evaluate GEO experiments, analyze idealo's visibility against relevant competitors, and translate findings into concrete optimization measures. You continuously assess emerging GEO tools, methodologies, and platform capabilities to improve our approach.

  • AI Shopping & Content Optimization: You explore how idealo's product, pricing, and offer data can become a valuable information source for AI agents and agentic commerce. Together with Content Marketing, you assess existing content and develop answer-focused, well-structured formats that strengthen relevance, authority, and citation potential.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing: You connect technical SEO and GEO requirements with Product and Engineering initiatives and collaborate with Brand and Communications/PR on authority-building and digital PR opportunities. You actively share your expertise, communicate findings to stakeholders, and contribute insights from the evolving AI search landscape to idealo's long-term SEO strategy.



Skills & Requirements

  • 3-5 years of hands-on SEO experience, with a clear focus on technical SEO. 

  • Strong technical SEO fundamentals: site architecture, crawlability, indexing, Core Web Vitals, JavaScript SEO, and experience running full technical audits. 

  • Practical understanding of how generative search systems retrieve, summarize, and cite content.

  • Experience with data analysis, KPI definition, and translating data into recommendations. 

  • Hands-on proficiency with core SEO tools (Google Search Console, GA4, Ahrefs or Semrush, Screaming Frog or similar crawler). 

  • Familiarity with structured data, semantic models, and entity-based SEO. 

  • Experience with GEO/AI visibility tools (e.g., Profound, AirOps, Rankscale, Peec AI, Otterly). 

  • Strong AI mindset: willing to test new GEO tools and methods and share learnings with the team. 

  • Excellent communication skills, able to present technical findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Content, Brand, and Communications/PR. 

  • Experience in e-commerce, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SQL or reporting automation with tools such as n8n are a plus.

title: Technical Product Manager, Integrations
description:
Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

The role

Most enterprises will never call our API directly. They will meet TabPFN inside the platforms they already run: SAP, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Databricks, or their own cloud. How well that works, how fast each release arrives there, and which platforms come next is the job of our Technical Product Manager for Integrations.

You take each model release from handover to live across every channel, working with the engineers who build the model and the partner teams who host it. Inside SAP you carry the product side of TabPFN across its platforms, from AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud, and you help build the integration engineering team that will work with you. Several decisions are yours to bring to the table: which announced channels we build next, what a marketplace listing should cost, how support for all of this works.

You work directly with our product team, our engineers and the founders, and you report to the CTO. This suits someone who enjoys landing things on a date as much as deciding what to build, and who still likes being close to the code.

What you'll do

  • Take every model release live across SAP, the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, on a plan you build with product and engineering.

  • Be the technical counterpart for the partner teams that host TabPFN, from SAP's platform teams to the hyperscaler marketplaces.

  • Shape how TabPFN shows up inside SAP's stack and what the integration engineering team builds first.

  • Bring the open channel decisions to the founders with a recommendation, and stay hands-on: listings, docs, smoke tests, a PR when it is faster than asking.

What we're looking for

  • Two or more years as product manager for a platform or integration surface: a product that ships into partners' platforms, or that other companies build on.

  • You have shipped through gates you did not control, landed multi-team releases on dates, and made a large enterprise's process work for a small, fast team.

  • You started as an engineer and never fully stopped: you read code, logs and scan reports without a translator.

  • You are in Berlin or ready to relocate; Freiburg or New York can work.

What sets you apart

  • You have shipped into an SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft or Oracle ecosystem, or know the cloud marketplaces from the inside.

  • You have deployed machine learning models and know what GPUs cost.

  • You have worked at a startup, and you use AI tools to take real work off your plate.

Life at Prior Labs

You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.

Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.

Our Commitments

The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.
