description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

We're expanding access to affordable credit by launching credit products that make a real difference to customers. We move quickly, often with leading fintech, consumer and e-commerce companies, so that we can offer affordable credit at the right point in the customer journey. We work in a highly regulated environment, so our products have to work end to end from day one: technically, operationally and commercially.

 

As a Product Associate, you'll work across product, data and commercials. You'll dig into how our products perform, from funnel conversion to loan-level unit economics, and turn what you find into ideas for how we scale, improve margins and grow. You'll work hands-on with data and code, alongside Product Managers, Engineering, Credit and Operations. You'll help decide where the product goes next, as well as how we ship it.

 

This role is for top-tier STEM or Economics graduates who think like analysts, build like engineers and care about the P&L like owners, and who want to progress to Product Manager at a fast-growing, industry-leading fintech.

 

What you'll be doing

 

Product analytics & insight

  • Own analysis of product performance across the full funnel: traffic, applications, approvals, conversion, originations, repayment and credit outcomes

  • Build and maintain the dashboards, metrics and data models that Product, Credit and Operations rely on

  • Form sharp hypotheses, design experiments (journey changes, pricing, A/B tests) and measure the impact rigorously

  • Get to the root cause of anomalies quickly, whether the cause is in the data, the code or the customer journey

Unit economics & commercial thinking

  • Model the economics of each product: acquisition cost, approval and take-up rates, pricing, funding cost, expected loss, servicing cost and lifetime value

  • Put numbers on the trade-offs behind product decisions, such as wider approval versus higher losses, or partner revenue share versus volume

  • Track contribution margin and cohort profitability by product, channel and partner, and show where we make or lose money

Growth & product strategy

  • Come up with ideas for scaling and growing from where we are today (new segments, channels, products and pricing) and estimate what each one is worth

  • Look across our products and partnerships for places where they reinforce each other: cross-sell, top-ups, repeat lending, shared customers and shared data

  • Help evaluate new partner opportunities and build the business case, covering volume, economics, integration effort and risk

  • Turn the strongest ideas into clear proposals and see them through to launch

Building & shipping

  • Use AI coding tools to build and ship product end to end, across both front-end and back-end, from quick prototypes to features that go live

  • Build internal tools, automations and data workflows that remove manual work and help the team move faster

  • Be proficient with our analytics stack: build dashboards in AWS QuickSight and track funnels, events and experiments in PostHog

  • Use SQL and Python every day to pull, model and analyse data

  • Learn how our APIs, decisioning flows and data pipelines work, and work directly with engineers on specs, testing and release validation

  • Support Product Managers with discovery, delivery and partner onboarding

Launch readiness & operations

  • Define success criteria for each launch and the metrics that show whether it's working

  • Design test scenarios, including edge cases and failure modes, and test the end-to-end customer journey before release

  • Work closely with QA to make sure production releases are stable

  • Monitor production performance after release, and pick up and triage related bugs with engineering

  • Make sure new products and journeys work at launch for customer support, collections and complaints teams

  • Use operational data to spot recurring issues, fix them at the source and make sure they're closed out, not just discussed

Who you are

  • A top-tier STEM or Economics graduate (computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, economics or similar)

  • 0–2 years of experience, including internships, placements or early-career roles with real responsibility

  • Strongly analytical and confident with SQL and Python, able to go from raw data to a clear recommendation

  • Able to build with AI. You use AI coding tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) to ship working front-end and back-end code, and you've built things, whether side projects, hackathons, internal tools or production apps

  • Hands-on with analytics tools such as AWS QuickSight, PostHog or similar BI and product analytics platforms

  • Commercially minded. You naturally ask how something makes money, and you enjoy modelling unit economics, pricing and P&L

  • Strong product sense. You have opinions on the products you use, why they work and how they could grow

  • A structured problem-solver who can break down messy, real-world problems

  • A clear communicator who can walk an engineer through a model and make a recommendation to leadership

Nice to have: an interest in consumer credit, lending, payments or fintech; experience with experimentation and statistics.

How you work (and what we value)

  • You think like an owner, of both the customer outcome and the commercial outcome

  • You'd rather build a quick prototype or run the numbers than debate in the abstract

  • You follow through until problems are actually solved

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity and don't wait for perfect instructions

  • You speak up when something doesn't make sense, and you help fix it

  • You put in extra effort at key moments, such as launches and live incidents, knowing that's where the real learning happens

Progression & growth

This role is a stepping stone to Product Management, with a clear progression path. As a Product Associate, you'll be expected to:

  • Build deep knowledge of our products, data and commercials

  • Consistently own problems end to end and deliver measurable business and customer impact

  • Show strong judgement, data-driven thinking and stakeholder management

High performers will progress to Junior Product Manager as they begin to:

  • Own a product area or metric independently, including its commercial performance

  • Lead defined workstreams within launches or partner integrations

  • Originate growth ideas that make it onto the roadmap and deliver results

Progression is based on impact and ownership, not time served.

What we offer

  • 2 paid volunteering days per year

The Role

We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen.

This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off.

We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you.

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the Express / Mid-prime product: proposition, roadmap, performance and economics, with direct accountability for the balance between growth and credit quality.

  • Lead how we quote and present offers across aggregator and price-comparison marketplaces, optimising eligibility, risk-based pricing and offer presentation to win the right customers at the point of acquisition.

  • Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book.

  • Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

  • Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

  • Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

  • Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

  • Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science.

  • Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

  • Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

  • Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

Who you are

  • A product person at heart: you care about the customer, the journey and the commercial outcome, and you want to own something end to end.

  • Quantitative and hands-on. You are comfortable in SQL and Python (or similar), you can interrogate a dataset yourself, and you can hold your own in a conversation with data scientists about model performance and calibration.

  • Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending.

  • Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance.

  • Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth.

  • Able to move between detail and direction: happy getting into the data on a Tuesday and shaping the roadmap on a Wednesday.

  • Confident challenging assumptions and turning analysis into practical action, and able to explain your reasoning clearly to people who are not analysts.

  • Collaborative and credible with risk, commercial, engineering and data science teams.

  • Structured, proactive and comfortable in a scaling environment where priorities evolve quickly and ownership is expected.

Experience and background

  • Around four to five years of experience in product, credit strategy, analytics or a closely related role within consumer lending or fintech. We are deliberately targeting this level: this is a step-up role for someone ready to own a product, not a lateral move for someone who has run several.

  • Experience in unsecured consumer lending, ideally Unsecured Personal Loans (UPL), with exposure to the mechanics of acquiring customers through price-comparison or aggregator marketplaces. Direct experience in higher-APR or near-prime lending is a strong plus but not a prerequisite.

  • Hands-on data skills: SQL as a minimum, and ideally Python or R for analysis. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be able to work alongside them as a peer and do your own analysis.

  • Experience working with or alongside credit decisioning, scorecards or risk models, and an understanding of how they are built, monitored and adjusted for a specific population.

  • Some experience of pricing, eligibility or offer design, and of using experiments or A/B tests to evaluate changes.

  • A track record of using analysis to influence decisions, not just to report on outcomes, in a role where you had some accountability for commercial results.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to senior stakeholders.

  • Experience with Open Banking data or cashflow underwriting is a plus, as is experience in a fast-growing fintech.

About the Role 🤔

Conversion is one of the three chokepoints in our revenue organisation. Customers arrive, take the demo, go through KYC, and too many stall before the first purchase, or buy once and never come back. The second purchase is where the product becomes sticky, and getting a merchant there is the hardest 60 days of their life with us.

Fixing that takes two things, and this role owns both. Reps who know the product, the pricing and the playbook cold. And a conversion funnel that is measured, scored and coached rather than hoped for.

 

Function one: enablement

Training and standards

  • Make sure every rep is up to spec and trained, and keep them there.

  • Own the theoretical onboarding of every new rep, SDR, AE and AM alike: what Nivoda sells, to whom, at what price, and how.

  • Set what "up to spec" means for each role and hold the bar.

Documentation and materials

  • Own the product material for every line of business: how it works, who it is for, pricing, take rate and best practice.

  • Keep it current. A rep should never be the last person to find out something changed.

The channel to marketing

  • Act as the link between marketing and the front line. Every campaign is known to the reps in advance, socialised at the all-hands before it lands, not discovered from a customer.

The channel to product

  • Translate the product roadmap into enablement. You do not decide the roadmap. You turn it into what to sell, to whom, and when.

  • When something ships, the reps already know what it is and how to position it.

Function two: conversion

Conversion rests on two things, and this role owns both: the call, and the KYC. A brilliant call that dies in KYC converts nothing, and a clean KYC on a badly run call never gets there.

Call scoring

  • Build the scoring rubrics with the team managers, so the standard is one both sides recognise.

  • Run transcript review and scoring at volume, using Claude to do it.

  • Send the reports out every week, to everyone.

  • Run a weekly leaderboard: the best calls, the scores, winners and losers, visible to the team.

  • Build a personalised coaching plan for every rep, written down and tracked, not delivered verbally and forgotten.

  • Coach in two directions: with the managers so they can coach their own people, and directly with reps where that is faster.

KYC

  • Own the insight generation of what is working and not on the process

  • Hold the accountability of the KYC SLAs, and call it out when they slip.

  • Map the blockers and the escalation paths, and push the fix at the cause rather than the symptom, across sales, product and marketing as needed.

  • Make sure the KYC operators know the rules, and that the rules are written.

  • Train and enable both sides of it: the reps and the operations team.

How we will measure it 💻

  • Conversion through to second purchase at 75% of each new cohort.

  • KYC above 60%, in every geography, not just on the average.

  • Rubric and call scores in place and reported weekly.

  • 80% compliance against the rubric, reached by your fourth month in the role.

What do we need from you? 💪

  • Experience in sales enablement, revenue operations or frontline sales coaching in a transactional, high-volume environment.

  • You have scored calls at volume and can show what changed as a result. Gong or equivalent.

  • You are fluent with AI tooling and would run transcript review and scoring through Claude rather than by hand.

  • You have built onboarding for reps from scratch, not just delivered someone else's deck.

  • You can coach a manager, not just a rep. You are comfortable telling a senior person their team's calls are not good enough, and then showing them how to fix it.

  • You write clearly. A large part of the value here is documentation other people can pick up and use.

  • You work across Product, Marketing and Finance without authority over any of them.

  • Hands-on. This is not a strategy seat. You will be on calls, in the CRM and in the material every week.

title: Robotics Engineer
description:
Help shape the future of robotics in construction.

ABOUT XYZ REALITY

XYZ Reality created the world’s first and only engineering-grade augmented reality solution, purpose-built for the construction industry. Our holographic technology sits within The Atom, a smart, site-safe headset and hardhat, and is used on live projects to ensure schemes are delivered on time and on budget.

XYZ has grown to over 150 staff across the UK, US and Europe, and works with mission-critical organisations and construction companies to deliver major projects.

THE ROLE

Construction sites are some of the hardest environments for robot autonomy: they change every day and are full of clutter, obstacles and people. XYZ Reality’s robotics programme is extending our technology toward robots that can operate reliably in them, from autonomous data collection and construction progress capture through to executing construction tasks.

We’re looking for a Robotics Engineer to make that real. You’ll work hands-on with robot hardware in our London office, using a modern stack (ROS 2, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, learning-based control), and see your work tested in real construction environments, not just in simulation.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor role focused on robot software and algorithmic control, backed by a good working knowledge of robot hardware. If you have strong robotics fundamentals from an MSc, PhD or applied research group, love making systems work on real robots, and want your ideas to shape the direction of a programme, we want to hear from you.

This is an office-based role at our London site in Angel, Islington.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Integrate robots with XYZ’s software, bringing up ROS / ROS 2 interfaces, robot control, sensors, compute and data flows, and building repeatable tools for bring-up, configuration, logging and monitoring.

  • Establish reliable baseline control and develop task-specific behaviours for navigation, positioning and capture, training and tuning control policies in simulation and validating them on hardware.

  • Develop localisation-aware path planning, waypoint execution and obstacle handling, working with project and site teams to turn work plans and BIM-derived locations into robot missions.

  • Integrate capture payloads so images, pose, timing and mission status flow reliably into XYZ’s construction progress workflows, working with navigation, SLAM and perception colleagues.

  • Design test scenarios and measure mission completion, coverage, localisation quality, intervention, recovery and repeatability, improving the system through measured iterations.

  • Bring technical expertise and new ideas to the programme, comparing scripted, motion-planning and learning-based approaches and helping shape what comes next.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • MSc or PhD in Robotics, Controls, Computer Science, Mechatronics or a related discipline, or equivalent applied robotics experience. Industry experience is not required.

  • Hands-on experience building, programming or directly controlling a physical robot, from an academic project, research lab or industry.

  • Strong Python and C++, practical ROS experience (ideally ROS 2) and working knowledge of kinematics, coordinate frames, feedback control, state estimation, path planning and robot hardware.

  • Experience training or tuning robot control policies (e.g. reinforcement or imitation learning) using NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim or similar tools, with a rigorous experimental approach.

  • The right to work in the UK. We’re unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

KEY EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

  • ROS / ROS 2, Python & C++

  • Robot control, kinematics, state estimation & path planning

  • NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim, reinforcement or imitation learning

  • Sim-to-real transfer on physical hardware (desirable)

  • Navigation, SLAM, perception & sensor fusion (desirable)

  • Mobile or field robotics, BIM/CAD or construction technology (desirable)

BENEFITS

🏝️ 25 days annual leave + public holidays
🩺 Private healthcare with Vitality
🎄 Christmas shutdown days on top of leave allowance (2–4 per year usually)
🚇 Office located within a 5-minute walk from Angel station
🪙 Annual salary reviews
🥳 Summer & Christmas staff parties
🍣 Free lunch on Thursdays, followed by after-work drinks
💰 Employee referral scheme
🚀 Make a real-world impact by helping transform the construction industry

title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).

  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

description:

Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team - from Finance to HR - to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.

With a team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, we've raised nearly $400M from top-tier investors and were named a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software.
 
At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

Reporting to the CISO, you'll own the security roadmap for Pigment's product, infrastructure, and CI/CD environment, and you'll build much of it yourself.

This is a hands-on role: expect to read code, threat model new services, reproduce and triage vulnerabilities, dig through infrastructure configuration and build the automation that closes gaps.

You'll also set direction and bring product and engineering with you, but that influence comes from technical credibility and not process: the engineers you work with will take you seriously because you've been in the same code they have.

The scope is broad: application security, infrastructure security, detection and response, and the assurance work that keeps our certifications standing. You won't be covering it alone. The security team is seven people and growing, with colleagues already owning compliance, governance and security operations, so this role can go deep on product and infrastructure and not be spread too thin across everything. Nobody arrives fluent in all of it: we're looking for real depth in several of these areas and the judgement to grow into the rest.


Key responsibilities include:

  • Product & Infrastructure Security Design - Design security features into the product itself and strengthen defence-in-depth across the platform. Threat model new services before they ship, and make the architectural calls that are expensive to reverse later.

  • Security Review & Risk Assessment - Review code, architecture and configuration yourself, and be the person developers and PMs bring problems to early rather than late. Deliver solutions that balance risk against business benefit, and escalate the calls that genuinely need senior arbitration.

  • Assurance & Testing - Run our assurance programme: internal code, architecture and configuration reviews, red team exercises, and the bug bounty. Own the relationship with third-party auditors, and measure the control KPIs that keep our certifications defensible.

  • Vulnerability Management - Own vulnerabilities from detection through to verified fix: reproduce them, score and triage them, design or validate the mitigation, and confirm it actually worked. Improve the KPIs that tell you whether the process is holding.

  • Detection Engineering - Build and improve our detection capability alongside the infrastructure and engineering teams: identify the signals worth collecting, write rules that catch real attacks without drowning us in noise, and build the response playbooks behind them.

  • Incident Response - Lead security investigations into the production environment end to end, from first signal to root cause, across incidents and fraud. Flag the repetitive work worth automating and the detections worth building, and hand those to the security operations team.

  • SDLC - Set the technical direction for how engineers at Pigment build securely: guidance, paved paths, and reviews that teach and not just gate. Contribute to company-wide awareness where it counts, but your primary audience is product, engineering and SRE.

 

Example projects that would fall under your responsibilities (actual examples of recently completed or currently on the roadmap):

  • Secure the design and development of our AI features, including the MCP Server and Modeler Agent: threat modelling, design reviews, working alongside the engineers building them, and security assessments. 

  • Work out where AI-assisted analysis actually belongs in our pipeline. AI-powered security reviews reason about a diff semantically rather than pattern-matching it, which is genuinely different from classic SAST - but it's not a drop-in replacement, and figuring out the split between AI review, traditional SAST and SCA is an open question we'd like you to answer with evidence rather than vendor claims.

  • Migrate GitHub to managed identities: provisioning through Okta, retiring personal accounts and long-lived PATs, and moving CI to short-lived OIDC credentials instead of stored keys.

  • Design agent identity for the MCP Server - delegated access tokens, token exchange, and making sure an agent acting for a user can never exceed what that user could do themselves.

  • Push least privilege further across production and CI/CD. Better than it was, not where we want it.

For a concrete example: here's how we built a sandboxed execution environment for LLM-generated code.

Technical Environment

Mostly production, with the occasional internal IT-adjacent project: 

  • Main sites in Paris, London, Toronto and NYC 

  • MacOS, Windows, Linux workstations

  • GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, Postgres, SingleStore, Vault

  • Okta, OAuth, JWT, C#, .NET Core, TypeScript, React, Python, Go

  • Datadog (SIEM), CloudFlare ZTNA, Falco, Wiz, Riot, HackerOne, TruffleHog

  • Google Workspace, Jumpcloud, Vanta, Hibob, Slack

  • GitHub, CircleCI, ArgoCD

  • SOC 1, SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 42001

Who you are

You have at least 8 years of experience in security as a Security Engineer, Pentester or Security consultant, with real depth in product and/or infrastructure security. We care more about the scope of what you've owned than the exact number of years.

What you've done

  • Owned a security roadmap for a product or platform end to end, rather than delivering items on someone else's

  • Driven security work through engineering teams you had no authority over

  • Been the person your organisation escalated to on hard architectural calls

  • Worked hands-on across a broad technical surface - development, databases, networking, web

How you work

  • You're hands-on and intend to stay that way (this position does not include people management)

  • You look for the workable answer, not the blocking one

  • You have a good dose of humility, and you help the people around you get better

  • You speak English fluently, French is a strong plus

After a first call with our recruiter, five conversations, around four hours in total, usually over two to three weeks:

  1. Ways of working (45 min) — how you operate with people, and what draws you to this role specifically.

  2. Technical deep dive (1h30) with a security engineer — including a practical. We'll give you a real problem we've already solved and talk through how you'd approach it.

  3. Cross-functional (45 min) with an engineer from product or platform — someone who'd be on the receiving end of your work.

  4. Ownership and career (1h) with the CISO and a member of the security team.

  5. Final (45 min) with our co-founder and CTO.

title: Senior AI Support Engineer (Paris)
description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

Support at Dust is not a cost center. It is one of the most important product surfaces we own.

As a Senior AI Support Engineer, you will help define what world-class support looks like in an AI-native company. You will not just resolve tickets. You will own the systems, agents, workflows, and feedback loops that make support better, faster, and more scalable over time.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who has already operated close to support strategy, technical escalation, user experience, and automation. You should be excited by the idea of taking recurring customer pain and turning it into durable systems: better agents, better documentation, better internal tooling, sharper product feedback, and fewer repeat issues.

The best person for this role is not a traditional support leader who wants to manage a queue from a distance. It is someone with strong technical instincts, a deep user mindset, and a track record of building support systems that change how a team operates.

You might be a great fit if you have built an AI-powered support function, owned support tooling at scale, worked deeply with LLMs or automation, or carried a support strategy from problem discovery through implementation and measurement.

What you will own

Building the AI systems that make support scale

You will design, build, and continuously improve the AI-powered systems that help Dust support customers with speed and quality. This includes agents for ticket classification, auto-acknowledgement, response drafting, internal routing, proactive incident detection, knowledge retrieval, and escalation support.

You will identify categories of recurring issues and engineer them out of the support queue. Sometimes that means building a better Dust agent. Sometimes it means improving documentation, creating an internal tool, tightening a workflow, writing a script, or escalating product feedback upstream with enough context for engineering to act.

You will be expected to measure whether the systems you build actually improve the user experience. Seniority here means not just shipping tooling, but knowing what good looks like, instrumenting it, and iterating until the impact is visible.

Running complex support when the systems fall short

You will still be close to the work. You will investigate complex customer issues across logs, code, internal tooling, product behavior, and agent outputs. You will provide clear, accurate answers to customers, including when the underlying issue is ambiguous or technically complex.

You will handle escalated cases with precision and judgment, communicating clearly with both technical and non-technical users. You should be comfortable translating between customer language, product behavior, engineering detail, and business impact.

When AI-generated responses are incomplete, inconsistent, or wrong, you will debug the system behind them. You will improve prompts, knowledge sources, workflows, routing, tooling, and escalation paths so that the same failure mode does not repeat.

Shaping the support strategy

You will help define how Dust should run support as we scale. That means thinking beyond the queue and owning the full loop: what customers experience, what support sees, what agents can handle, what engineering needs to fix, and what product should learn.

You will translate repeated customer pain into high-quality product signal. You will build strong working relationships with engineers and product teams so escalations are high-context, actionable, and efficient.

You will also help raise the bar for how the support function operates: what we measure, how we prioritize, how we review quality, how we onboard junior team members, and how we decide what should be automated versus handled by a human.

What we are looking for

Every candidate and employee’s success at Dust is measured against the same three dimensions: Aptitude, Attitude, and Agency.

Aptitude

You have strong technical depth. You are comfortable with APIs, web applications, logs, scripts, and internal tools. You can navigate a codebase, reason through product behavior, and troubleshoot systems without being stopped by a stack trace.

You have genuine AI fluency at builder level. You have built agents, automations, workflows, or internal tools using AI systems such as Dust, Cursor, Claude Code, n8n, GPT-4, Claude, Mistral, Gemini, or similar platforms. You are not just good at prompting. You understand how to turn AI into operational leverage.

You have experience operating at the strategy layer of support, not only at the ticket layer. You have owned or helped shape support systems, support tooling, escalation workflows, deflection strategy, knowledge management, or AI support operations.

You can balance technical accuracy with user experience. You care about whether the customer understood the answer, whether the product pain was addressed, and whether the issue will happen again.

You are able to communicate bidirectionally: clearly enough for customers, technically enough for engineers, and strategically enough for leadership.

Attitude

You combine resilience with empathy. This is a front-line role, and customer frustration is often direct and unfiltered. You do not take it personally, but you do take it seriously.

You are proactive rather than reactive. You do not wait for a perfect problem statement from the customer. You investigate, infer, clarify, and anticipate what they may need next.

You have strong prioritization judgment. You know what needs an immediate human response, what can be automated, what should be escalated, and what should become product feedback.

You are comfortable setting boundaries. You do not say yes to everything, and you can explain tradeoffs clearly in a way that builds trust rather than eroding it.

You care about the craft of support. You see support as a product experience, not a back-office function.

Agency

You turn patterns into systems. When you see the same issue twice, you start asking whether it should exist at all.

You go deep before escalating. You investigate as far as you reasonably can, so that when you involve engineering or product, they receive a clear problem statement, relevant evidence, and a useful recommendation.

You build without waiting for permission. If you see a gap in the support system, you are excited to prototype, test, and ship a better version.

You continuously improve your own workflows. You treat your time, your tools, and your operating system as things worth debugging.

You extract product opportunities from customer interactions. You do not let support signal disappear into a solved ticket. You close the loop.

What strong candidates may have done before

You may have:

  • Built or led an AI-powered support function

  • Designed support agents, internal copilots, escalation workflows, or deflection systems

  • Owned technical support tooling, support operations, or automation at a fast-growing software company

  • Worked as a senior support engineer, technical support engineer, developer support engineer, support ops engineer, solutions engineer, or implementation engineer

  • Built a support product, internal platform, AI startup, or automation-heavy support system

  • Operated in a high-volume environment where quality, speed, and judgment all mattered

We care more about the depth and relevance of your experience than the exact number of years. That said, we expect this role to be a fit for someone who has already spent several years close to technical support, support engineering, AI tooling, or support systems ownership.

What this role is not

This is not a traditional customer support role focused only on ticket resolution.

It is not a people-management role where you are far away from the technical work.

It is not a pure operations role where you optimize process without building.

It is not a role for someone who is curious about AI but has not yet built with it.

The person we are looking for should be excited to own the messy middle between customers, AI agents, internal tooling, engineering, and product.

Compensation and benefits

  • Competitive compensation

  • Significant equity package in a Sequoia-backed startup

  • Substantial relocation support, up to 10k€, including help finding an apartment in Paris and support with the visa process

  • Health insurance for you and your dependents

  • New MacBook Pro or Linux machine, monitor, keyboard, and equipment

  • Beautiful office in the heart of Paris

  • Opportunity to travel to the US multiple times a year

  • Regular team events and offsites

We can go higher for exceptional profiles.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Act as the primary relationship owner and escalation contact for Contract Manufacturers (CMs) and specialized board and harness fabricators, overseeing supply continuity, risk mitigation, price negotiations, and the transition from New Product Introduction (NPI) to full scale Mass Production (MP).

  • Work across internal functions to fulfill rapid prototyping needs, meet hardware build milestones, resolve technical bottlenecks, and integrate novel vendor technologies.

  • Lead operational initiatives around integrating new and adapted electronics technologies, delivering technical briefings and progress updates to executive leadership.

  • Establish vendor evaluation systems to track key performance metrics across quality, operational execution, cost variance, and continuous innovation.

Candidate Requirements

  • Educational Background: Master's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • Relevant Experience: 6+ years of specialized experience managing electronic commodities (PCB/PCBA, custom cabling, wire harnesses) within a high tech sourcing or supply chain engineering environment.

  • Technical Aptitude: Advanced proficiency in Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) modeling and data driven vendor evaluation within complex hardware architectures.

  • Commodity Strategy: Demonstrated ability to craft clear commodity strategies in direct collaboration with engineering leadership.

  • Proven Leadership: Strong cross functional leadership skills, with a track record of driving alignment across diverse teams.

  • Adaptability & Mobility: Highly adaptable, hands on professional who thrives in a fast paced, dynamic environment, bridges operational gaps, and removes process friction.

  • Communication & Influence: Excellent written and verbal communication, capable of engaging a wide range of stakeholders, from junior members to senior executives.

  • Sector Exposure: Prior exposure to defense, aerospace, automotive, or high reliability technology sectors is strongly preferred.

  • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI's mission, vision, and ambitious growth plans, ready to go the extra mile to ensure operational excellence.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

description:
ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE :

École du ministère en charge de l'industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines- Télécom, 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l'avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses 4 missions - former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l'innovation - en un cercle vertueux et porteur d'innovation.

Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche la place IMT Mines Albi comme école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT, à savoir l’industrie du futur responsable, l’énergie, économie circulaire et société ainsi que l’ingénierie, santé et bien-être.

IMT Mines Albi s‘est dotée en 2023 et pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en 7 grandes actions, répondant ainsi aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT à laquelle elle appartient.

IMT Mines Albi, au travers du Centre Génie Industriel (CGI), développe des recherches à la frontière entre l’intelligence artificielle et le génie industriel, en collaboration avec des partenaires publics et industriels nationaux et internationaux.

Le Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) (https://cgi.imt-mines-albi.fr/) compte environ 70 personnes dont 25 doctorants. Le centre s’intéresse à l’accompagnement de la transition des écosystèmes en permettant de prendre des décisions responsables et durables, dans des environnements instables ou perturbés. Ceci est mis en pratique par la représentation, la modélisation et l’analyse des données de ces organisations afin de formaliser de la connaissance conduisant à la prise de décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs, incertains et/ou perturbés.

Le CGI est structuré selon des axes de recherche appliquée et des programmes scientifiques. Les axes de recherche appliquée sont :

  • Axe FLOWS : Flexible Logistics and Operations for sustainable WorldS dans lequel ce poste est rattaché.

  • Axe DiSCS : Digital Systems for Crisis management and Security ;

  • Axe TRACE : Territorial Resilience, Agility, and Circular Economy ;

  • Axe WHOPS : Well-being and Health through Organizational Processes and Services.

Les deux programmes scientifiques au cœur de ces axes de recherche sont :

  • HOPOPOP : Hybridization for Operations & Planning, Organizations & Performance, Optimization & Problem-solving ; 

  • AIME-DM : Automated Information Modeling and Extraction for Decision-Makers.

 

DESCRIPTION DU POSTE :

Dans le contexte de l’Education 4.0, les différents acteurs d’un établissement de formation universitaire (étudiants, personnels, intervenants extérieurs, etc.) ont des contraintes et des objectifs différents ce qui rend complexe la coordination et le pilotage de tels établissements (organisation et planification des enseignements, gestion des espaces collectifs, organisation des sessions d’examens…).

En complément, ces établissements doivent s’adapter tant sur la gestion de leurs sites (meilleure adéquation à de nouvelles formes pédagogiques) que sur les flux de personnes les utilisant pour une meilleure répartition des charges et une interopérabilité de tous les outils à disposition (par exemple, un gestionnaire d’emploi du temps). Dans ce cadre, le jumeau numérique organisationnel représente le système qui permet une simulation et une aide à la prise de décision par des échanges bidirectionnels entre l’organisation physique (personnes et systèmes dont les bâtiments) et sa réplique virtuelle dans un objectif de pilotage global des flux.

Le projet DIGIFAC’Santé s’inscrit dans ce contexte. Il porte sur la conception et le développement d'un jumeau numérique des sites d’une université, de la gestion des flux étudiants et personnels et de l’évolution pédagogique de ses formations.

Un jumeau numérique ne peut remplir son rôle qu'à la condition de représenter fidèlement les informations essentielles à la prise de décision, elles-mêmes issues de données collectées dans les différents services de l’Université et des applications logicielles actuelles. Or, ces applications présentent des niveaux d’hétérogénéité différents selon leurs fonctionnalités. La nature des opérations réalisées (emploi du temps, gestion des salles et du matériel, etc.) impose des contraintes fortes sur la disponibilité de ces données : leur collecte automatique et en temps réel n'est pas toujours techniquement envisageable, ce qui constitue un défi central pour l'alimentation du jumeau numérique.

L’étude à mener dans le cadre de ce projet vise à :

Modéliser le besoin informationnel. Il s'agit de concevoir un méta-modèle capable de représenter, de façon générique et formelle, les informations strictement nécessaires à l’alimentation du jumeau numérique universitaire. Ce méta-modèle doit permettre de cadrer la remontée d'information en définissant le juste besoin, c'est-à-dire en distinguant ce qui relève de l'information décisionnelle de ce qui constitue un artefact de collecte sans valeur ajoutée pour le pilotage.

Alimenter les modèles. Une fois le méta-modèle du besoin informationnel établi, la question de son instanciation à partir de données réelles des applications existantes se pose. Comment alimenter ces modèles à partir de données hétérogènes, partielles, et produites selon des rythmes et des modalités de collecte variables ? Ceci articule des enjeux d'intégration, de qualité et de cohérence de la donnée au regard des exigences du jumeau numérique.

Gérer l'absence de certaines données. Dans un contexte où certaines opérations ne permettent pas une collecte automatique et en temps réel, en raison de la nature même des processus mis en place (par exemple, construction de l’emploi du temps, suivi des cohortes d’étudiants), comment maintenir la cohérence et la complétude de la représentation portée par le jumeau numérique ? Ce lot interroge la capacité du système à pallier les lacunes de la remontée de données par des mécanismes d'inférence ou de déduction, permettant de reconstituer un état vraisemblable du système à partir d'informations partielles.

Proposer des aides au dimensionnement et au pilotage des sites universitaires. Il s’agit ici d’utiliser le jumeau numérique dans toutes ses fonctionnalités afin entres autres de s’assurer que les évolutions bâtimentaires envisagées permettent d’accueillir l’ensemble des flux actuel et projeté pour cet établissement, de permettre d’optimiser les flux entre les différents sites et de valider les choix d’évolution des pratiques pédagogiques et leur adéquation vis à vis des capacités disponibles (salles et équipements spécifiques, surfaces, personnels,etc.).

Compétences, connaissances et expériences souhaitables :

  • Modélisation des processus / d’organisation

  • Analyse systémique

  • Analyse de données

  • Ingénierie dirigée par les modèles

  • Aide à la décision

  • Simulation à évènements discrets et jumeau numérique

  • Fouille de processus (process mining),

  • Des connaissances en algorithmique, UML, Web sémantique seront très appréciées

Capacités et aptitudes :

  • Anglais écrit et parlé (Niveau B2 minimum exigé) ; cf. référentiel européen ; ex. :  785/990 minimum au TOEIC), attesté par une certification reconnue (TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS).

  • La maîtrise du français (C1 minimum) est exigée afin de faciliter les échanges avec les experts et les acteurs.

  • Capacité à travailler dans une équipe de recherche, autonomie, esprit d’initiative, organisation, curiosité intellectuelle…

  • Motivation pour contribuer à une application universitaire

 

PROFIL RECHERCHE :

Ingénieur.e recherche ou post-doctorant, en génie industriel et/ou supply chain management et/ou Génie Logiciel ou Master ou équivalent (niveau Bac+5).

 

AU-DELÀ DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT PROFESSIONNEL, POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE ? :

title: Directeur des opérations Datacenter (H/F)
description:
Head of DC Operations (H/F)

Région parisienne

Votre mission

Dans un environnement où la disponibilité et la fiabilité des infrastructures sont essentielles, Isatalent recherche un(e) Head of DC Operations pour piloter les opérations de ses data centers en région parisienne.

Rattaché(e) à la direction, vous êtes garant(e) de la performance opérationnelle, de la continuité de service et de la fiabilité des infrastructures. Vous encadrez les responsables de site et travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d'expertise centrales, les clients et les partenaires de maintenance.

Dans un contexte de croissance de l'entreprise et d'exigences opérationnelles, vous jouez un rôle clé dans l'harmonisation des pratiques, la structuration du pilotage des activités et l'accompagnement du changement auprès des équipes.

Votre objectif : construire une vision opérationnelle consolidée, maîtriser les risques et fédérer les équipes autour d'exigences communes de performance, de sécurité et de qualité de service.

Vos responsabilités

Piloter la stratégie et la performance des opérations multisites

  • Élaborer une feuille de route opérationnelle à court et moyen terme, en définissant les priorités, les plans d'action et les ressources humaines et financières nécessaires.

  • Définir et harmoniser les méthodes de pilotage des activités opérationnelles sur l'ensemble des sites.

  • Consolider et faire évoluer les KPI et tableaux de bord portant notamment sur la disponibilité des infrastructures, la maintenance, la communication client et le respect des procédures.

  • Analyser les résultats, identifier les écarts de performance et piloter les actions correctives.

  • Produire un reporting structuré à destination de la direction et éclairer les décisions stratégiques.

Manager les responsables de site et accompagner la transformation

  • Encadrer et accompagner les responsables de site dans le pilotage de leurs activités et le développement de leurs compétences.

  • Apporter une expertise opérationnelle et technique permettant de challenger les choix, les priorités et les plans d'action.

  • Favoriser l'autonomie, la responsabilisation et la coopération des équipes.

  • Organiser l'allocation des ressources et le suivi des plans de charge.

  • Accompagner la réorganisation du périmètre, harmoniser les pratiques et contribuer à l'intégration de nouveaux sites.

  • Travailler en transversalité avec le responsable du pôle Expertise et les autres fonctions de l'entreprise.

Garantir la fiabilité des infrastructures et maîtriser les risques

  • Garantir la disponibilité, la résilience et la continuité d'exploitation des infrastructures critiques.

  • Superviser la maintenance préventive, corrective et réglementaire, ainsi que les travaux, extensions, rétrofits et changements réalisés en environnement exploité.

  • Reprendre et consolider la cartographie des risques opérationnels et techniques, notamment les points uniques de défaillance (SPOF) et les obsolescences critiques.

  • Hiérarchiser les risques, définir les plans de traitement, en évaluer les impacts financiers et humains et identifier les investissements nécessaires.

  • Piloter les incidents majeurs, les escalades, les analyses de causes et le suivi des actions correctives et préventives.

  • Garantir le respect des exigences de sécurité, de conformité et de continuité de service.

Développer la relation client et le partenariat avec les mainteneurs

  • Garantir le respect des engagements contractuels, des SLA et des standards de qualité attendus par les clients.

  • Renforcer la qualité de la communication opérationnelle et la confiance avec les interlocuteurs clients.

  • Développer une relation constructive et partenariale avec les mainteneurs et les prestataires.

  • Améliorer la coordination des interventions, le suivi des engagements et la qualité des prestations.

  • Identifier les axes de progrès et piloter les actions d'amélioration de la performance des partenaires.

Piloter les budgets et l'amélioration continue

  • Élaborer et suivre les budgets OPEX et CAPEX du périmètre.

  • Arbitrer les priorités de maintenance, de renouvellement et d'investissement en fonction des risques, des capacités et des engagements clients.

  • Garantir le respect des exigences réglementaires, environnementales, HSE, ICPE et des référentiels ISO applicables.

  • Déployer des standards, procédures et méthodes de travail homogènes.

  • Contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance énergétique des installations, notamment du PUE, et à la maîtrise des coûts d'exploitation.

Votre profil

Formation et expérience

  • Formation supérieure, idéalement Bac +5, de type ingénieur ou master spécialisé en génie électrique, énergétique, climatique, maintenance industrielle ou management des opérations. Un Bac +3 technique pourra être étudié au regard d'une expérience particulièrement solide.

  • Expérience significative dans l'exploitation, la maintenance ou la direction technique d'infrastructures critiques.

  • Expérience significative en management de managers, en pilotage multisite ou dans une fonction de responsabilité opérationnelle comparable.

  • Expérience confirmée dans un environnement critique fonctionnant 24h/24 et 7j/7, avec de fortes exigences de disponibilité, de sécurité et de conformité.

  • Expérience en gestion d'incidents majeurs, pilotage de budgets, gestion des risques et conduite de transformations opérationnelles.

Compétences techniques

  • Bonne maîtrise des enjeux d'exploitation des data centers et compréhension des architectures électriques, mécaniques, CVC, de protection incendie, de GTB/BMS et des systèmes de contrôle.

  • Maîtrise du pilotage de la maintenance préventive, corrective et réglementaire.

  • Connaissance des SLA, KPI de disponibilité, capacité, qualité de service et performance énergétique.

  • Capacité à analyser et challenger les risques techniques, les plans de maintenance et les investissements.

  • Maîtrise des enjeux budgétaires OPEX/CAPEX et des exigences réglementaires applicables.

Qualités personnelles

  • Leadership et capacité à manager des responsables expérimentés.

  • Crédibilité technique et sens des responsabilités.

  • Capacité à structurer une organisation, harmoniser les pratiques et conduire le changement.

  • Aptitude à fédérer les équipes et à développer la coopération transverse.

  • Capacité de décision, d'arbitrage et de priorisation.

  • Sang-froid en situation de crise, rigueur et orientation résultats.

  • Sens du client et capacité à construire des relations de partenariat durables.

Langues : français courant et anglais professionnel, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Les enjeux de réussite

Au cours des premiers mois, vous aurez notamment pour objectifs de construire une feuille de route opérationnelle claire, de consolider le pilotage par les indicateurs, de hiérarchiser les risques et de définir les moyens nécessaires à leur traitement.

Vous contribuerez également à renforcer la cohésion managériale, à harmoniser les pratiques entre les sites et à accompagner l'évolution de l'organisation dans une logique durable de performance et d'amélioration continue.

Tasks

  • Own a product domain end-to-end. Depending on where you'll have the most impact, that could be alerting, on-call and call routing, status pages, integrations, or our AI SRE. You propose what to build, build it, and measure whether it worked.

  • Make the scope calls. Decide what to cut, what ships first, and what to validate before building it. We trust you with these trade-offs.
  • Own it in production. You're responsible for what you ship, including when it breaks. Reliability is literally our product.

What you bring

  • 2+ years of software engineering in a team codebase. That means code review, tests, production incidents, and code you didn't write alone. Side projects are great, but they don't replace this.
  • You've shipped features end-to-end and cared whether people actually used them.
  • Comfortable across the stack. Strong on one side, and willing and able to work on the other.

  • Product instinct. You have opinions about what to build, not just how.

Bonus

  • Experience at a B2B SaaS or developer-tools company

  • Hands-on with Java, Rust, React or TypeScript
  • Something you built that other people actually use (open source, a side project, an internal tool)
  • German language skills

Benefits

  • 🧭 Real Ownership: You decide what to build in your domain, not just how to build it.

No cover letter needed. Send your CV along with:

  2. A few lines on which part of ilert you'd want to own first, and why.

If you're the kind of engineer who has opinions about what to build, not just how to build it, we want to talk to you.

description:
Senior Software-Entwickler (m/w/d) – PHP/Symfony & React – Berlin

Der Plan steht, jetzt fehlst du: Bring unsere Software von Legacy-PHP auf Symfony und React.

Auf einen Blick

Die Rolle

Unser Kernprodukt Konsentas ist über viele Jahre gewachsen, und das sieht man dem Code an. Das Backend läuft auf PHP 8.1 ohne Framework. Im Frontend stehen jQuery und Vanilla-JS neben React, und automatisierte Tests gibt es bisher wenige.

Wohin es gehen soll, ist klar: Das Backend wird schrittweise auf Symfony umgestellt, das Frontend auf React vereinheitlicht. Bis Ende 2027 soll die Migration abgeschlossen sein. Was dafür fehlt, ist kein Plan, sondern Kapazität.

Du triffst eigenständig technische Entscheidungen, bringst dich in Architektur- und Modernisierungsfragen ein und sorgst dafür, dass die Codequalität mit jedem Release besser wird. Dabei bleibt das Produkt im Einsatz: Wartung, Support und neue Features laufen parallel zur Modernisierung.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Legacy-Module bei laufendem Betrieb schrittweise durch Symfony-Services und React-Oberflächen ersetzen

  • Fullstack-Features von der Datenbank bis zum Frontend entwickeln, teils auch als kundenspezifische Erweiterungen

  • Bestehenden Legacy-Code pflegen, debuggen und weiterentwickeln

  • Gelegentlich an Kundenterminen teilnehmen, etwa alle 3–4 Wochen

Nach 6 Monaten …

… setzt du Features eigenständig um, hast spürbar zur Modernisierung beigetragen, die Codequalität verbessert und bist für unsere Azubis eine feste Ansprechperson.

Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung: etwa 4–5 Jahre in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung (ein Richtwert, keine harte Grenze)

  • PHP: fundierte Kenntnisse in modernem PHP 8.x mit objektorientierter Architektur, etwa Dependency Injection, Interfaces und SOLID

  • Symfony: nachweisbare Praxiserfahrung mit dem Framework

  • Legacy-Code: Du gehst sicher mit gewachsenen Codebasen um. Du refaktorierst, debuggst und entwickelst weiter, ohne alles neu zu schreiben.

  • JavaScript/React: solide Erfahrung im Frontend, jQuery schreckt dich nicht ab

  • Datenbanken: relationale Datenbanken wie MySQL/MariaDB oder SingleStore und sicherer Umgang mit SQL

  • Tooling: Git und Arbeit mit CI/CD

  • Sprache: Deutsch auf C1-Niveau, Englisch mindestens B1

  • Arbeitsweise: eigenständig, strukturiert, proaktiv und mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch

  • Persönlich: Du kommunizierst verlässlich, arbeitest gern im Team, übernimmst Verantwortung, hast keine Angst vor schwierigen Codestellen und gibst dein Wissen gern weiter.

  • Abschluss: Ausbildung oder FH-Abschluss zählen bei uns genauso viel wie ein Uni-Studium. Entscheidend ist deine Praxiserfahrung.

Pluspunkte: REST/API-Design und Schnittstellenentwicklung, automatisiertes Testing (PHPUnit, Jest), Docker, Deployment-Pipelines und Cloud, Software-Architektur und Design

-

Patterns, produktiver Einsatz von KI-Tools wie Claude Code oder Codex. Erfahrung mit Software für den öffentlichen Sektor ist nicht nötig.

Ein kleines Team mit kurzen Wegen: Daniel (Developer Lead), Nico (Geschäftsführer & Projektmanager), der selbst aktiv mitentwickelt, ein externer Entwickler und zwei Auszubildende. Ihr stimmt euch täglich ab. Daniel und Nico übernehmen dein Onboarding persönlich.

  3. Teamgespräch vor Ort

  4. Angebot

Über Girona

Seit über 25 Jahren entwickelt die Girona Softwareentwicklung GmbH in Berlin Software für die öffentliche Verwaltung. Städte wie Berlin, München, Bonn und Dessau setzen seit Jahrzehnten auf unsere Lösungen, Konsentas etwa in Bürgerämtern, Gesundheitsämtern sowie Kfz-Zulassungs- und Führerscheinstellen.

title: (Senior) Finance Manager (all genders)
description:
At Klim, we work with farmers and food companies to make regenerative agriculture scalable and financially rewarding for farmers. Through our platform, we help farmers restore soil health, increase biodiversity and capture carbon while creating new, reliable income streams.


We’re a Berlin-based AgriTech startup backed by $22M in Series A funding, partnering with global food leaders such as Nestlé and Kaufland to reduce emissions across their supply chains and build long-term resilience. Since 2020, we’ve supported 3,500 farmers managing over 900,000 hectares.

If you’re passionate about building a sustainable food system and driving real climate impact, join us and help create a healthier planet!

Your mission:

As our (Senior) Finance Manager, you will run all aspects of Finance at Klim. From HGB accounting and the monthly and annual close, through day-to-day financial operations, to audits, controlling and finance projects — you own the full breadth of the finance function end-to-end. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with unusually broad responsibility: you are the person who keeps our financial engine room running accurately, reliably and on time, and who continuously makes it simpler, faster and more automated. You are supported by a working student whose work you steer, and you report directly to our COO.

This role is a great fit for you if you are a finance all-rounder who wants genuine ownership of the entire finance function and the opportunity to make a real impact from day one. With a broad mix of strategic, tactical and operational responsibility, you’ll have plenty of room to shape how we work, improve what’s already there and build an automated Finance function.

Your responsibilities:

  • Own our HGB-compliant accounting: run the month-end and year-end close and deliver accurate, timely financial statements with our external accountants.

  • Run financial operations end-to-end: accounts receivable and payable, tax-compliant invoicing, payment runs, expense flows and cash management.

  • Manage statutory reporting and tax topics (e.g. Jahresabschluss / annual financial statements, VAT) together with our external tax advisors.

  • Prepare and manage the annual audit: audit files, documentation and communication with auditors.

  • Support controlling and strategic finance topics: management reporting, analyses and spreadsheet-based models that inform business decisions.

  • Be the driving force behind the introduction of innovative AI-based processes, building a state-of-the-art efficient and effective finance setup.

  • Manage and develop our finance working student.

Your profile:

  • 3–5 years of experience in accounting and/or finance roles.

  • Solid HGB accounting experience, including month-end and year-end close.

  • Hands-on experience in financial operations (invoicing, payments, expense management, cash).

  • Very diligent and reliable: high attention to detail, structured, and on top of many short- and long-term deadlines.

  • You are highly autonomous and have a hands-on mentality: you are comfortable owning the full breath of the finance function. You take responsibility for getting things done and you are very good at collaborating with internal and external stakeholders.

  • Experience driving innovation and AI in Finance: You have designed, optimized and automated processes and are confident using AI tools.

  • Fluent in German and English (written and spoken).

Your benefits:

  • Opportunity: Be part of our journey from the very beginning, working on an equal footing with the leadership team to build a new company.

  • Impact: Make a daily and active contribution to combating climate change, promoting consumer education, and fostering fair conditions for our climate-conscious farmers.

  • Autonomy: Take ownership of your projects and enjoy a high degree of creative freedom.

  • Flexible work model: At Klim, we foster a flexible, hybrid work approach and facilitate remote work (within the EU). It is advantageous for this role if you live in Berlin or can be present in our office regularly.

  • Additional benefits for Germany-based employees: We offer a subsidy for a membership in Urban Sports Club or the Deutschlandticket, a company pension scheme, plus team lunches (if based in Berlin) and regular team events.

At Klim, we believe that a thriving workplace is built on the diverse backgrounds, talents, and perspectives of our team. We grow stronger together by embracing and building on each individual’s unique strengths.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute their best. All hiring and personnel decisions are made solely based on qualifications, performance, and the needs of the company - ensuring fairness and equal opportunity for all.

If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for our team in ways you don’t yet realize!

description:
Co-Founder | Growth, Community & Partnerships (m/w/d)

Standort: München (überwiegend vor Ort)
Start: Voraussichtlich Februar/März 2027
Compensation: EXIST Gründungsstipendium, 2.500 € monatlich für Hochschulabsolventen, plus geplante Beteiligung am Unternehmen

Über uns

Wir sind Pierre-Louis Suckrow und Kerim Anater. Unsere akademischen und beruflichen Hintergründe liegen in Informatik, Design & Computation und Human Computer Interaction. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir eine neue Plattform für die Organisation und Zusammenarbeit in der digitalen Musikproduktion.

Unser Produkt soll es ermöglichen, verschiedene Projektstände und ihre Entstehung nachzuvollziehen, frühere Versionen wiederherzustellen und Projekte zwischen unterschiedlichen Produktionsumgebungen auszutauschen. Damit möchten wir mehr Raum für musikalisches Experimentieren schaffen, den organisatorischen Aufwand in kreativen Arbeitsprozessen reduzieren und die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Musikschaffenden erleichtern.

Ein erster funktionsfähiger Prototyp für Ableton Live existiert bereits. Wir sind Teil des WaveLab Inkubators Batch #7 und im Wintersemester Teil der Munich Music Labs. Aktuell bereiten wir unsere Bewerbung für das EXIST Gründungsstipendium vor.

Zur Ergänzung unserer technischen und produktorientierten Kompetenzen suchen wir ein drittes Gründungsmitglied, das insbesondere die Kommunikation nach außen, den Aufbau von Kontakten und die Entwicklung von Kundenbeziehungen mitgestaltet.

Deine Rolle

In der kommenden Projektphase stehen die Weiterentwicklung des Produkts, die Validierung mit potenziellen Nutzern und der Aufbau erster Kundenbeziehungen und Partnerschaften im Vordergrund.

Wir suchen eine Person, die diese Prozesse begleitet und insbesondere den Austausch mit Menschen außerhalb unseres Teams übernimmt.

Mögliche Schwerpunkte sind:

  • Communications & PR: Entwicklung unserer Außenkommunikation, Vermittlung unserer Produktidee und Aufbau von Sichtbarkeit innerhalb der Musikbranche und darüber hinaus.

  • Community Building: Aufbau und Betreuung einer Community aus Musikproduzenten, Musikschaffenden und weiteren potenziellen Nutzern.

  • Partnerships & Networking: Kontaktaufnahme und Beziehungspflege mit Studios, Unternehmen, Branchenakteuren und potenziellen Kooperationspartnern.

  • Customer Discovery & Success: Durchführung von Gesprächen mit potenziellen Nutzern, Begleitung erster Beta User und Pilotprojekte sowie systematische Erfassung von Feedback.

  • Growth & Business Development: Mitentwicklung unserer Go to Market Strategie, Erschließung erster Kundengruppen und Validierung unseres Geschäftsmodells.

Die genaue Aufgabenverteilung möchten wir gemeinsam und abhängig von deinen bisherigen Erfahrungen und Interessen entwickeln.

Als drittes Gründungsmitglied bist du darüber hinaus an der strategischen und unternehmerischen Entwicklung des Vorhabens beteiligt.

Wen wir suchen

Wir suchen eine kommunikative und eigenständig arbeitende Person, die gerne mit Menschen in Kontakt tritt und Interesse daran hat, ein technologisches Produkt von der frühen Entwicklung bis zum Markteintritt zu begleiten.

Idealerweise bringst du Folgendes mit:

  • Erfahrung in einem kommunikationsorientierten Bereich, beispielsweise PR, Marketing, Community Management, Customer Success, Sales, Account Management oder Business Development.

  • Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Ideen verständlich zu kommunizieren und unterschiedliche Zielgruppen anzusprechen.

  • Freude am Aufbau und an der Pflege von Kontakten und langfristigen Beziehungen.

  • Eigeninitiative, organisatorische Fähigkeiten und die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

  • Interesse an digitalen Produkten, Technologie und kreativen Arbeitsprozessen.

  • Interesse an der gemeinsamen Gründung und langfristigen Entwicklung eines Unternehmens.

Nice to have, aber keine Voraussetzung:

  • Erfahrung in der Musikindustrie oder Kontakte zu Musikproduzenten, Studios, Labels oder Artists.

  • Erfahrung mit Startups, Software Produkten oder dem Aufbau von Communities.

  • Eigene Erfahrung oder Interesse im Bereich Musikproduktion.
