title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
description:
At CesiumAstro, we are developers and pioneers of out-of-the-box communication systems for satellites, UAVs, launch vehicles, and other space and airborne platforms. We take pride in our dynamic and cross-functional work environment, which allows us to learn, develop, and engage across our organization. If you are looking for hands-on, interactive, and autonomous work, CesiumAstro is the place for you. We are actively seeking passionate, collaborative, energetic, and forward-thinking individuals to join our team.

We are looking to add a Senior Mechanical Engineer to our Mechanical Engineering team. If you enjoy working in a startup environment and are passionate about developing space hardware for leading-edge communications satellites, we would like to hear from you. 

In this position, you will be responsible for mechanical design aspects of Cesium phased array antennas, subsystems, and interfaces through all phases of the development process. The ideal candidate will be versatile and proficient in mechanical analysis, electronics packaging, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical interfaces, thermal architecture, spacecraft propulsion, deployable and actuated structures, and environmental qualification of spacecraft antennas and payloads. You will be responsible for mechanical designs from concept through space flight including requirements definition, architecture trades and block diagrams, analysis, manufacturing, testing, qualification, and in-orbit support. 

The successful candidate will also present engineering design review materials to our customers and executive team, as well as participate in proposal-writing efforts. As such, excellent written and verbal communication skills are required. 


JOB REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor of Science (BS) in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering from an accredited university or institution 
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in space antenna and payload mechanical engineering to include electronics packaging, thermal, shock, vibration, stress dynamics, and cost. A Master's degree may count as two years of experience. 
  • Experience in conducting architectural trade studies including parametric and first-order cost and physical analysis 
  • Experience with professional mechanical and FEA CAD tools, such as Ansys Mechanical, SolidWorks Simulation, and Thermal Desktop 
  • Experience with CNC manufacturing and GD&T 
  • Experience with advanced aerospace manufacturing and materials including sandwich panels and carbon composites, OR experience with high-reliability deployment mechanisms for space applications (including deployment, HDRMs, power delivery, etc.).
  • Proficiency in detailed mechanical design (3D CAD, drawings, etc.) 
  • Experience designing and manufacturing mechanisms and mechanical actuators 
  • Experience with EMI/EMC mitigation techniques 
  • Familiarity with satellite thermal architectures including heat pipes, phase change materials, contact resistance, and surface finishes as well as fundamental understandings of orbital thermal control in a LEO environment. 
  • Familiarity with launch and LEO environments (thermal, shock, vibe, radiation, etc) 
  • Familiarity with design for test, manufacturability, assembly, and reliability 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills 

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE
  • Python, C++, or other programming languages 
  • Experience with large, deployable antenna arrays which drive your vision for the next generation of on-orbit communications and sensor arrays.
  • Robotics and control systems experience 
  • PCBA experience.

title: Data Privacy Analyst - Regulatory Compliance
description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Compliance team’s mission is to keep iwoca a safe and trusted lender for UK small businesses, and to make the compliant path the easy path for the teams we work with.

We make sure iwoca meets its regulatory obligations, particularly the financial crime, sanctions and data protection requirements that apply across our suite of products and services.

We are the second line of defence for the UK business. We advise the people building and running the business on what the rules require, set the policies and standards they work to, and test whether what happens in practice matches them. We work alongside the product teams so that each product meets its obligations and can grow.

Data protection is central to what we do. We hold the data privacy function for the UK business and own how iwoca handles personal data end to end: the lawful basis for how customer, applicant and third-party data is used; data subject access requests and other individual rights; personal data breaches; retention and deletion; records of processing; marketing and consent; the privacy review of new products and features; and the governance of automated decisioning and AI tooling.


How we work:

  • We enable rather than block. The answer is rarely just “no” — it’s what it would take to get to yes, and what the firm is accepting if it goes ahead anyway.

  • We go to the source. Positions are grounded in the actual rule, regulation or guidance, and we can show where they come from.

  • We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake.

  • We’re close to the business. We work directly with Tech, Data, Credit, Operations and Legal, and we want to be in the room early rather than at the end.

The role

As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing.

The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver.

There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business.

You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator.

Impact and influence

  • Individual rights and data breaches. Own data subject access requests from intake to response — scoping the search, applying exemptions and meeting the statutory deadline — along with erasure, rectification and objection requests. Triage and investigate suspected personal data breaches, assess them against the 72-hour notification test, and keep the breach register accurate.

  • Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows. Be an accessible first point of contact for teams across iwoca with a data protection question, and give them an answer they can act on, early enough to shape what they build.

  • Records, policies and reporting. Keep the record of processing activities accurate as the business changes, hold the retention and deletion schedules to account, review data processing agreements with suppliers, help maintain our data protection policies and standards, and produce the privacy reporting that goes to senior stakeholders.

  • AI and automated decisioning. Help assess AI tooling and automated decision-making across lending and operations: what personal data goes in, what lawful basis supports it, what the model does with it, and what rights customers have over the outcome. That includes the risks specific to these systems — decisions taken without meaningful human involvement, bias in outcomes, unreliable model output — and recommending how we address them.

  • Automation and improvement. Identify the manual steps in our privacy operations that should not be manual, assess the options, and set out the requirements and compliance implications clearly enough for Tech and Data to deliver them.

The requirements

Essential skills

We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Pricing to build the analytical and machine learning capability that pricing runs on, from demand modelling through to the systems that recommend price.

  • Develop machine learning models for demand forecasting and willingness-to-pay, and take them from exploration through to production with the monitoring and retraining that keeps them honest.

  • Move us from predictive to prescriptive by building the optimisation layer that turns forecasts and elasticities into recommended prices under margin, competitive and partner constraints.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

Why we're hiring

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

 

About the role

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

  • Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

  • Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

  • Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

  • Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

  • Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

  • Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

 

What this role isn't

  • An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

  • A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

  • A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

  • A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

  • A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

 

What success looks like

In your first 90 days:

  • The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

  • Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

  • You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

  • Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

  • At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

  • We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

  • You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

  • The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

  • Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

  • Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

 

About you

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

  • You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

  • You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

  • You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

  • You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

  • You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

 

How you will grow

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

 

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

  • 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

  • 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

  • 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

  • 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

  • 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

 

The environment

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

How we build (worth reading before the role)

How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.

We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.

We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

 

About the role

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.

Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.

That's also what makes it exciting.

You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.

Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.

Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product".

Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.

 

What matters most

We need all of these at once:

  • Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.

  • Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea.

  • Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked.

  • Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see.

  • Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features.

  • Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's.

And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it.

  • Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution.

  • Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense.

  • Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built.

  • Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst.

  • Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck.

 

About you

You'll likely thrive here if:

  • You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention.

Nice-to-haves:

  • You were a software engineer before you moved into product.

  • You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces.

  • You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off.

This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned.

 

How we work

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first.

Team

For this position, you will be an integral part of a newly established internal studio, a dynamic and focused team dedicated to one of our most promising prototype in scale. This studio is specifically chartered to improve this high-potential game up to the successful and market-ready title it is meant to become.

You will be part of the team building Draft Showdown, a turn-based multiplayer game, working alongside its client engineers and game designers as a full member of the game team. You will be part of a small group owning the backend that this game needs as its requirements become more specific and demanding.

You’ll also be plugged into Voodoo's shared gaming backend platform - the same architecture and patterns that power titles like Mob Control and Block Jam 3D - building on it and contributing back, in close collaboration with the wider backend team. You get the focus and ownership of a dedicated game engineer with the leverage and support of a battle-tested platform behind you.

This is a pivotal hire: Draft Showdown is moving towards competitive multiplayer, which means moving game logic from the client to the server. They are also implementing cheat detection safeguards to the game.
You will be central to that transition.

Role

You will design and build the server-side foundation that takes Draft Showdown from a client-authoritative game to a competitive, server-validated one. The current game computes everything on the device - progression, economy, and match outcomes alike, which won't hold up for competitive PvP. Your job is to change that.

Working closely with client developers and game designers from feature design through delivery, validation and iteration, you will:

  • Build server-side validation for the metagame - currency, card upgrades, chest opens, and progression - staged by risk, replicating economy and reward logic on the server.

  • Move toward server authority for competitive features, where game state lives in one place and can be trusted.

  • Implement and improve matchmaking and cheat detection safeguards for a Deterministic lockstep PvP architecture

  • Design APIs and player-state management that the Unity client integrates against, and help shape how client and server split responsibilities.

The responsibilities are cross-functional, ranging from infrastructure, API design & coding all the way to client-side integration (we are using Golang).

To succeed in this role, you will need to have passion for everything you do. You love to write code that scales to millions of users, are skilled at requirements gathering, champion new tech initiatives & leverage existing solutions.

  • Strong knowledge of computer science fundamentals

  • Background in high-scale systems

  • Understanding of Unix-like environments

  • AI-first mindset: Comfortable using AI daily and building custom agents or reusable automations to speed up your work

  • Strong analytical skills with a track record of solving complex problems related to scalability, performance, and integration in high-stakes environments.

Son équipe pluridisciplinaire et multiculturelle développe des solutions technologiques innovantes au service de l'efficacité, de la protection de l'environnement et de la maîtrise des coûts. L'entreprise est certifiée ISO 9001 et toutes ses activités respectent sa démarche QHSE.

Le poste

Votre rôle : mettre au point de véritables méthodes d’essai. À partir d’un besoin de mesure (température, pression, déplacement, déformation, ultrasons…), vous concevez, instrumentez et validez des cellules d’essais haute température et haute pression. Vous commencez par fiabiliser une cellule existante : simplifier son montage et son démontage, puis la valider à plus haute température. Vous lancez ensuite les cellules suivantes.

Vous travaillez avec l’équipe qui conçoit aujourd’hui les équipements, et avec le bureau d’études d’un fabricant partenaire qui réalise la conception détaillée et les plans de fabrication. Environ 70-80 % conception et développement, 20-30 % laboratoire. Rattachement à la direction des opérations.

Ce que le poste n’est pas : ni dessinateur ou calculateur (le détail et les plans sont externalisés), ni management d’équipe. 

Vos missions

  • Définir le besoin, le cahier des charges et le pré-dimensionnement fonctionnel de nouvelles cellules.
  • Choisir les capteurs adaptés et les intégrer ; résoudre les enjeux d’étanchéité, de tenue en température et en pression.
  • Consulter fournisseurs et sous-traitants, suivre la fabrication des pièces.
  • Monter, instrumenter et tester vous-même vos équipements au laboratoire ; interpréter les mesures et améliorer.
  • Améliorer l’ergonomie des équipements existants et transférer les équipements validés à l’équipe d’essais.
  • Rédiger la documentation technique et contribuer à la protection de la propriété intellectuelle.

Requirements

Indispensable

  • Conception mécanique d’équipements, avec une CAO 3D (aucun logiciel imposé).
  • Instrumentation, capteurs et techniques de mesure physique et physico-chimique : choisir et intégrer, pas fabriquer.
  • Goût du terrain : vous aimez monter, démonter et intervenir vous-même sur les équipements.

Important

  • Gestion de projet : planning, budget, fournisseurs.
  • Rigueur, autonomie, communication proactive des difficultés.

Un plus

  • Anglais technique (échanges écrits avec des fournisseurs étrangers).
  • Mise en plan, notions de matériaux et d’isolation thermique.
  • Expérience en pression ou température.

Formation et expérience

  • Diplôme d’ingénieur (bac +5) en mécanique, génie physique, instrumentation ou mesures physiques. Un parcours associant mécanique et mesures physiques (BUT Mesures physiques puis école d’ingénieurs en mécanique) est particulièrement apprécié.
  • Environ 5 ans d’expérience en conception d’équipements, bureau d’études ou R&D ; profils plus juniors étudiés.

Sur site. Manutention occasionnelle de pièces métalliques lourdes avec moyens de levage. Intéressement
Rémunération : 36 – 48 k€ brut annuel selon expérience

At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.

The opportunity

As an AI Unity Tools Engineer, you'll build the next generation of QA automation and development tooling for Homa's games. This is a new, high-impact initiative, and you'll own it: from the first question to the tools running in production across our portfolio.

You’ll work across AI, Unity, QA automation, DevOps, and infrastructure to make testing and build pipelines more reliable, scalable, and cost-efficient for games developed by Homa and its studios. You'll be working on AI-driven QA automation at the edge of what is technically possible, and you'll see the impact directly in the speed, reliability, and cost of how our games are made.

What you'll do

  • Build. Design and deploy AI-enabled QA automation pipelines across Homa's major Unity games.
  • Run. Maintain and improve our TeamCity build pipelines and infrastructure so game builds stay reliable.
  • Scale. Onboard new games and tools onto the platform without reducing service quality.
  • Explore. Test AI-driven approaches to QA that cut manual testing effort and reduce reliance on costly legacy tooling.
  • Drive adoption. Work with developers, QA teams, studios, and mobile teams so the tools you build are actually used.
  • Measure. Track the impact of your work on testing time, build reliability, and cost, and turn it into clear recommendations.

Requirements

  • Ownership. You drive outcomes. When a build breaks or a test fails, you fix it instead of explaining why it broke.
  • Proactive. You don't wait for instructions or perfect conditions. You spot what needs doing and do it.
  • Pragmatism and simplicity. You look for the simplest solution that works, use whatever tools are available, and ship. You turn ambitious ideas into practical, achievable solutions.
  • Sharp thinking. You learn fast, reason from facts, and structure your ideas clearly. You can explain a complex technical solution to developers, QA teams, and studios in a few sentences.
  • AI-driven. AI is already part of how you work every day. You've used it to automate, speed up, or rethink at least one thing you're proud of.
  • Hungry and motivated. You're ambitious, high-energy, and grounded. You see this role as a chance to build something new and grow faster than anywhere else, and you're ready to work for it.
  • Bonus: you've built something. An internal tool, a testing framework, a game, a side project. We'd love to hear about it.

For this role, you'll also bring

  • Hands-on experience with Unity and the ability to understand Unity games, game systems, and testing contexts.
  • Proven experience using AI systems, models, or AI-enabled engineering workflows in practice.
  • Strong DevOps understanding, including TeamCity, build pipelines, and infrastructure.
  • The ability to work across technical topics while understanding the wider product and business context.
  • Experience working in a complex environment with meaningful product and testing volumes.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience building QA automation or testing frameworks.
  • Experience with AI-driven exploratory testing.
  • Experience in gaming or another Unity-based product environment.
  • Experience supporting products with high testing volumes.
  • Experience driving adoption of internal tools across multiple teams.

Even if you don't check every box, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Why Homa

  • Exceptional growth. We hire people of outstanding potential, then put them where they can grow fastest.
  • Real ownership, early. This is a new initiative. Your tools will change how Homa and its studios build and test games, and you'll see the results.
  • A high talent bar. Our teams are small and demanding, and the people around you will push you to grow.
  • AI at the core. You'll have access to the best AI tools, and you'll help shape how an AI-first company works.

Benefits

Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here's what you can expect:

  • 🏥 Comprehensive Benefits: Depending on your location, you'll enjoy a range of perks such as insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym memberships, and more.
  • 🏢 Paris HQ Access: Enjoy a desk at our private office in a well-located WeWork building that will give you access to WeWork perks like rooftop view and designed coworking spaces.

Own the definition of operational readiness for go-live: what "ready to run in production" means, how the bank proves it at each regulatory gate, and what has to change in the organisation for that proof to hold.

The bank's operations teams, processes and provider contracts were built to run classical banking infrastructure. Agentic AI workloads need a different operating model, and you will shape it: redraw responsibilities between the client's teams and its managed service providers, set the standards each party works to, and lead the people through the change — so that those who run the platform today are ready and willing to run what comes next.

  • The incident and change path — set the runbook standard and its required coverage, extend incident classification and intervention mechanisms to agentic failure modes, and have rollback and change-failure rates measured and reported by those who own them

  • Comfortable operating in a complex, multi-stakeholder programme where scope and ownership are still being established across parallel workstreams

Wir begleiten Unternehmen von der Anforderungsanalyse über Architektur, Softwareentwicklung und Implementierung bis hin zum Betrieb. Mit rund 800 Kolleg:innen in Deutschland, Polen, Litauen, Rumänien und Indien verbinden wir technologische Exzellenz mit Branchenkompetenz in Automotive, Handel, Banken & Versicherungen sowie dem öffentlichen Sektor.

Wir begrüßen Bewerberinnen und Bewerber, die sich bereits mit modernen KI-gestützten Entwicklungstools und generativer KI beschäftigen oder Interesse daran haben, diese sinnvoll in ihren Arbeitsalltag zu integrieren. Den reflektierten Einsatz von KI sehen wir als wertvolle Ergänzung zu technischem Know-how und eigenständigem Denken.

Als Data Analyst beantwortest du fachliche Fragestellungen eigenverantwortlich mit Daten: Du analysierst, modellierst innerhalb bestehender Strukturen, baust Dashboards und bringst deine Ergebnisse so auf den Punkt, dass Fachbereiche damit arbeiten können. Konzeption von KPI-Systemen und Datenmodellen gestaltest du mit – ohne sie allein verantworten zu müssen – und übernimmst Schritt für Schritt eigene Themenbereiche wie Datenqualität, Reporting-Standards oder Self-Service-Enablement.

  • Eigenverantwortliche Durchführung von Datenanalysen innerhalb bestehender Analytics- und BI-Lösungen – von der Klärung der Fragestellung bis zur Ergebnispräsentation

  • Übersetzung fachlicher Anforderungen in Auswertungslogiken, Kennzahlendefinitionen und prüfbare Hypothesen

  • Aufbereitung, Verknüpfung und Plausibilisierung heterogener Datenbestände mit SQL sowie Analysesprachen wie Python oder R

  • Durchführung explorativer und deskriptiver Analysen, etwa Mustererkennung, Segmentierung, Kohorten- und Zeitreihenanalysen oder A/B-Tests

  • Entwicklung und Pflege interaktiver Dashboards und Reports mit gängigen BI-Plattformen wie Power BI, Tableau, Qlik oder IBM Cognos, inklusive Modellierungs- und Formelsprachen wie DAX

  • Mitarbeit an der Konzeption von KPI- und Kennzahlensystemen sowie an wiederverwendbaren semantischen und Reporting-Layern

  • Analyse und Optimierung von Queries, Datenmodellen und Reporting-Workloads mit Blick auf Laufzeit und Nachvollziehbarkeit

  • Sicherstellung von Datenqualität durch Validierungsregeln, Reconciliation-Prozesse und Root-Cause-Analysen bei Auffälligkeiten

  • Umsetzung von Berechtigungs- und Row-Level-Security-Konzepten sowie Dokumentation von Datenmodellen, Transformationslogik und Geschäftsregeln

  • Einsatz KI-gestützter Werkzeuge und generativer KI zur Unterstützung von Analyse, Dokumentation, Tests und Qualitätssicherung – inklusive der KI-Assistenzfunktionen in BI-Plattformen

  • Adressatengerechte Aufbereitung von Ergebnissen für Fachbereiche und Projektstakeholder, inklusive Data Storytelling

  • Abstimmung mit Data-Engineering-Teams zu Datenbereitstellung, Schnittstellen und Modellanpassungen

  • Mitarbeit an Change Requests, Incident-Bearbeitung und Roll-outs neuer Features im Betrieb der Analytics-Lösungen

  • Unterstützung von Fachbereichen bei Self-Service-Analytics sowie Mitwirkung an Schulungen und Wissenstransfer

  • Unterstützung von Junior-Kolleg:innen im Tagesgeschäft und Teilnahme an Reviews


  • Abgeschlossenes Studium im IT-, MINT- oder wirtschaftswissenschaftlichen Umfeld (z. B. Wirtschaftsinformatik, Informatik, Mathematik, BWL) oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation

  • 3–5 Jahre praktische Erfahrung in Data Analytics, Business Intelligence oder Reporting

  • Gute bis sehr gute SQL-Kenntnisse sowie Erfahrung mit analytischer Datenmodellierung und Data-Warehouse-Strukturen

  • Praktische Erfahrung mit mindestens einer Analysesprache, idealerweise Python oder R

  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit mindestens einer BI- und Analytics-Plattform, z. B. Power BI, Tableau, Qlik oder IBM Cognos, inklusive Datenmodellierung

  • Methodenkompetenz in deskriptiver Statistik, Hypothesenprüfung und gängigen Analyseverfahren sowie Erfahrung in der Arbeit mit großen Datenmengen

  • Betriebswirtschaftliches Verständnis für Geschäftsprozesse und Kennzahlensysteme (KPIs)

  • Grundverständnis moderner Datenplattformen und Datenbereitstellungsprozesse, z. B. Azure, AWS, GCP, Databricks, Snowflake oder Microsoft Fabric, sowie von ETL-/ELT-Konzepten

  • Erfahrung in Datenqualität, Berechtigungskonzepten und der Dokumentation von Datenlogik

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Versionskontrolle (Git)

  • Offenheit für den reflektierten Einsatz KI-gestützter Werkzeuge im Analytics-Kontext

  • Erfahrung in agilen Arbeitsweisen (Scrum/Kanban)

  • Kommunikationsstärke und die Fähigkeit, analytische Ergebnisse verständlich zu vermitteln

  • Analytisches Denkvermögen, strukturierte Arbeitsweise und Freude an der Arbeit im Team

  • Deutschkenntnisse auf C1/C2 Niveau

  • Englischkenntnisse auf B2 Niveau

  • Wohnsitz in Deutschland, idealerweise Nähe Ratingen/Frankfurt

Dann bewirb dich trotzdem! Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

  • Erfahrung mit digitalem Performance Tracking, Produkt- oder Web-Analytics

  • Grundkenntnisse in CI/CD für Analytics-Artefakte

  • Interesse daran, eigenes Wissen in Workshops oder internen Formaten weiterzugeben

title: Engineering Manager
description:
Sunday creates pocket-sized friends for the mass market. We turn idle moments into meaningful connections for millions of users worldwide.

Sunday focuses on the psychology of care, companionship, and empathy. We build accessible worlds where players don't just solve puzzles, they rescue friends. By combining mass-market accessibility with deep emotional hooks, we are defining the next era of digital entertainment.

As Engineering Manager, you will lead Sunday's engineering team of approximately ten engineers across Unity game development and SDK. The position reports to the Director of Operations and works in close partnership with Production, Product, and Growth.

The role combines people leadership with technical ownership. Your primary responsibility is to lead and develop the team and to define how engineering operates. At the same time, you remain close enough to the code to own architectural decisions, review critical work and contribute directly where this supports delivery.

Our team delivers frequent releases across a portfolio of live games. We are looking for a leader who understands the trade-offs between quality, time and budget in the context of business priorities, and who translates them into sound technical decisions and the management of the team. This includes making our delivery pace sustainable through stable releases, a well-maintained codebase and engineering practices that scale with the business. The role carries a clear mandate to shape how engineering works at Sunday.

What you will own

  • People leadership: development plans, performance conversations against clear role expectations, hiring and onboarding. You hold conversations early and directly.

  • Engineering ways of working: code review standards, quality gates before release, build and release pipeline, and a deliberate plan to reduce hotfixes and technical debt.

  • Architecture and platform: owning the technical foundations shared across our games, including our in house SDK, analytics tracking, live configuration and the setup of A/B tests.

  • Delivery partnership: working with the producers who lead our cross functional game teams on estimates, capacity and technical risk, and having the final say on whether a release is technically ready to ship.

  • Transparency: making engineering progress, quality and capacity visible to the rest of the company through clear, measurable indicators.

What you bring

  • At least four years managing an engineering team of five or more people, including performance management and hiring.

  • A strong engineering background of your own, ideally in C#, Unity or mobile development, so you can lead architecture and review decisions with credibility.

  • A proven track record of success in a commercially driven company operating live products with real users, where engineering decisions are made against business priorities.

  • A track record of raising quality and delivery predictability in a small or fast moving company, with concrete examples of what you changed and how you measured it.

  • Comfort with direct conversations and with holding people to clear standards: Open, respectful, goal orientated.

  • A pragmatic, data driven approach: you decide based on what the numbers show, and you introduce the process only where it pays back.

Strong plus

  • Experience in frequent shipping of mobile games, ideally free to play, casual or hybrid casual titles.

  • Hands on knowledge of ad monetisation and mediation SDKs, mobile measurement partners and A/B testing infrastructure.

  • Experience introducing CI/CD, automated testing or release quality gates in a game studio.

Fuel for the Journey: Benefits to Support Your Ambitions

  • Invest in Your Future: Regular feedback and our development program support your growth, helping you expand your skill set and achieve your career goals.

  • Easy Arrival to Sunday: From signing to settling in Hamburg, we’ve got you covered. Need a visa? No problem. Ready to build your new life and career at applike in Hamburg? We support every ambition - from learning German to a relocation bonus that helps you settle in and make Hamburg feel like home.

  • Live Your Best Life, at Work and Beyond: We work in a hybrid setup with 3 core office days, plus flexible working hours. Enjoy 30 vacation days, 3 weeks of remote work per year, and free access to an in-house gym with lots of different fitness classes and mental health support through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

  • Thrive Where You Work: Enjoy the Alster Lake view from our central office with top-notch equipment, fun open spaces, and a large variety of snacks and drinks.

  • Join the Community! Participate in regular team and company events, including hackathons and social gatherings. We work together, and we celebrate together, too.

If you want to build the future of digital companionship, Sunday is your home. Apply now!

title: Senior DevOps Engineer (all genders)
description:
Sunday Natural is one of Germany’s fastest-growing natural health brands, and our eCommerce platform is growing with it – today it serves 7 million monthly active users, runs on €400k of AWS per year, and supports a development organization of 30+ engineers. Every one of those numbers has moved sharply upward in the last few years, and all of them will keep moving.

You would be our first dedicated in-house Senior DevOps Engineer – and the two biggest engineering projects of the next two years are yours to help define and drive: bringing our entire infrastructure under Terraform, and strengthening the scalability, security and compliance posture across our cloud environments.

Your role

  • You shape the infrastructure vision. How we run, deploy, monitor and scale is yours to define, propose and defend.

  • You work alongside our two external partners as the in-house technical counterpart – building the architecture and standards together, and bringing the deep platform knowledge back into the company. As the platform grows, taking the technical direction of that group is a natural next step, and one we would actively support.

  • You own our AWS spend – €400k a year that currently has no dedicated owner, including where it goes and how we bring it down.

  • You are the escalation point. When production is at risk, you decide.

  • You report directly to the Head of eCommerce Platforms, with direct access to leadership for the decisions that need it.

What you'll own

  • AWS infrastructure – EC2, RDS, Fargate, CloudFront, S3, IAM – plus Cloudflare, DNS and WAF

  • Security & compliance – DevSecOps practices, system audits, patching and access reviews, and GDPR-compliant data handling across every environment

  • Infrastructure as code – taking us from manually managed to fully Terraform-defined

  • Data layer – MySQL under production load: tuning, replication, and backups you have actually restored from

  • Cloud economics – a €350k annual AWS budget with real headroom for optimisation

  • Delivery for 30+ developers – Bitbucket Pipelines, environments, and how fast and safely code reaches production

  • Reliability at 7M MAU – monitoring, logging, alerting and incident response (New Relic, Sentry, CloudWatch, PagerDuty)

Your profile

  • 7+ years running production infrastructure, with deep hands-on AWS as the person accountable when it breaks

  • Security-conscious infrastructure operations – DevSecOps practices, system audits and access reviews, comfortable being accountable for GDPR-relevant data handling

  • Infrastructure as code at scale – Terraform as your default way of working, on an estate of comparable size

  • Deep Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) – you can trace a slow system from the kernel up and explain what you found

  • MySQL under real load – slow-query analysis, replication, indexing, tested recovery

  • Ownership of monitoring and incident response at scale – you have built the alerting that catches problems before customers report them, using tooling like New Relic, Datatog, etc. and run the on-call and post-incident process around it

  • Experience defining standards that other engineers work to, whether with in-house teams or external partners, and holding the line on them

Nice to have

  • PHP-FPM / Magento 2 performance tuning, or Varnish and Redis at scale

  • Cloud cost optimisation at six-figure annual spend

  • AWS architecture certification

  • Experience with SIEM tooling (e.g. Wazuh) or similar security monitoring

  • Background in direct-to-consumer eCommerce or other high-traffic system operations

Our stack

Magento 2 · PIM · PHP · MySQL · Redis · Varnish · Docker · AWS · Terraform · Bitbucket Pipelines · New Relic · Sentry · CloudWatch · PagerDuty · Cloudflare

What we offer

  • An appealing discount on all of our products – from essential oils to vitamins & nutrients

  • We offer 28 days of paid time off per year plus up to 5 days off between Christmas and New Year

  • The Urban Sports Club membership and either Swapfiets bike rental or a subsidy for the Deutschlandticket

  • We believe great things happen when we meet in person, which is why we embrace a hybrid model with one home office day per week – up to two depending on the area you are working in – and up to two weeks per year working from abroad

  • Receive various discounts of up to more than 50 percent on attractive brands such as Flaconi, Bosch, Apple or Expedia

  • You will be given real ownership and plenty of room for new initiatives, as well as the opportunity to contribute your expertise and implement your great ideas

  • We like to celebrate each other! Regular tea & office parties, Christmas and summer feasts and various influencer events such as Women's Day

We are looking forward to your application!

Sunday Natural emerged from a long-standing passion and research in the fields of health, healing, and personal growth. The lack of natural, high-quality products on the market was the original motivation for founding Sunday Natural in 2013. We aim to produce the products we ourselves would love to buy – as natural as possible, absolutely pure, free from any additives, and of the highest quality. In a strategic partnership with CVC, Sunday Natural is now one of Germany's most renowned quality manufacturers, with its own research and development department in Berlin. Our diverse team in Berlin consists of over 400 employees from more than 45 nationalities and continues to grow – but at a sustainable pace. Our goal is to foster a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive work environment with a diverse group of motivated, talented, and visionary team members.

title: Cloud Security Engineer
description:
YGO.ai is a VC-funded AI tourism platform. We are hiring a Cloud Security Engineer to own the security of our cloud platform, the APIs our enterprise clients run on and the company itself.


🛡️ About this role. The role carries two things at once. You own security engineering directly and hands-on. You build the security function around it as we grow. At YGO a pod lead is a squad leader and a spokesperson, close to the work and close to the client, rather than a full-time manager. You will not stop being an engineer.

The work is broad. You might review source code in the morning, investigate an endpoint alert after lunch and help design a new authentication flow the next day. You identify the highest-risk problems, decide what happens first and execute.

We serve major travel enterprises and we have enterprise commitments going live from the start of 2027. Security is a condition of that business, not a layer added afterwards.

🧑‍💻 What you'll own

  • Application security. Hands-on code and architecture review across our APIs, backend services and internal tooling. Targeted penetration testing to validate issues yourself. Working with engineers on root causes and practical fixes rather than handing over reports. Vulnerability management and the external penetration tests we commission

  • Detection and response. Knowing we are under attack while it is happening and what happens next. Alerting, intrusion detection, incident process and the on-call path

  • Cloud and platform hardening. Access control, network boundaries, secrets management, containers and the deployment pipeline. Security through the SDLC: CI/CD, repositories and dependencies

  • The security of our APIs. Authentication and authorization, tenant isolation, token scoping and lifecycle, abuse prevention, enterprise SSO and the audit trail our clients and our own accountability depend on

  • The security of our AI systems. Prompt injection, tool and agent permissions, our MCP server, retrieval and data ingestion. The data-residency rules we are held to contractually

  • Identity and company security. SSO, MFA and privileged access for employees, onboarding and offboarding, access reviews, MDM, endpoint security and SaaS access. The practical IT security a company our size needs done, not discussed

  • Secure design across the pods. Threat modelling and design review that enables engineers rather than gatekeeping them and raises the standard of what they ship

  • The security function itself. Set the priorities and the roadmap from actual risk, not security theatre. Decide what we build, buy, automate or leave for later. Grow the team and hire into it, represent security to enterprise clients and carry our SOC 2 programme on Drata. Compliance is part of the job and it is not the centre of it

🚢 What you'll secure

  • An AI search and recommendation engine for major travel enterprises: enterprise integration, SSO, client security reviews, GDS integrations

  • A content enrichment API sold as SaaS: high scale, public facing, data and AI heavy

  • The platform underneath: a client console with organisations, projects and API tokens, supplier and business-client integrations, data ingestion, an MCP server, and several LLM providers behind a single internal library

📚 Our stack

  • Backend: Go monorepo (no framework, 3+ services)

  • Data: PostgreSQL, Redis, Redis Asynq queue

  • Hosting: PaaS-managed containers, Cloudflare in front

  • Observability: Jaeger tracing, BetterStack for logging, alerting and on-call

  • Compliance: Drata, SOC 2 in progress

  • AI tooling: Claude Code, used across the whole team

✅ You must have

  • 5+ years of hands-on security work spanning more than one discipline. Not five years of engineering with some security in it. This role sets the standard for the company, so it needs someone who has seen enough to have judgement rather than opinions

  • Application security depth. You know how modern web applications and APIs are attacked. You can validate an issue yourself through code review or a targeted penetration test and work with the engineer on the fix

  • A strong grasp of authentication and authorization. OAuth and OIDC, sessions, token handling, access control and the failure modes behind most API breaches

  • Cloud security fundamentals, properly. Identity, network, workload and pipeline security on a modern cloud platform, applied to production systems you were responsible for

  • Defensive experience alongside the offensive. You have investigated real incidents. You have built or improved the detection and alerting that catches them

  • Threat modelling and secure architecture for cloud, container and API systems

  • An engineering background. You are comfortable in a codebase, you can review what our engineers and our AI tools produce and you can build what you need yourself. Our backend is Go. Prior Go experience is a plus and not a requirement

  • Comfort in resource-constrained environments. Startups, small security teams or consultancies taught you to prioritize on risk, business impact and available resources and to execute yourself

  • The appetite to build a team. You want to grow this function and eventually lead it. Prior leadership experience is a plus and not a requirement. We would rather have depth and develop the leadership than the reverse

  • Working proficiency with Claude Code. Share specific examples

  • Judgement about pace. You secure a company that ships daily without becoming the reason it stops. Guardrails over gates

  • Experience of SOC 2, ISO 27001 or demanding enterprise security reviews

  • Excellent spoken and written English. You will talk to auditors, client security teams and our own engineers, often in the same week

  • ⚠️ European or African time zones (±3 hours from CET)

  • Available full-time (40 hours per week)

🌟 Nice to have

  • AI and LLM security: prompt injection, agent and tool permissions, model security, retrieval pipelines. Very few security roles let you both use AI as your main tool and secure it as your subject. This one does

  • Early security hire experience. You have been the first or one of the first security hires at a startup or scale-up

  • Experience leading or mentoring security engineers

  • Go

  • Security tooling or automation you built yourself

  • MDM, endpoint protection and identity provider administration (Google Workspace or similar)

  • Compliance automation tooling (Drata, Vanta, Secureframe or similar)

  • Security certifications. Valued as a signal, never required

  • GDPR depth. Travel or GDS exposure

  • German

❤️ You are a great fit if you

  • See security as an engineering discipline. You ship fixes and guardrails, not slide decks

  • Can explain a vulnerability to an engineer and its business risk to a client's security lead in the same afternoon

  • Have done offensive work as a penetration tester or consultant and wanted broader ownership than producing reports

  • Want to build something and own it, rather than advise on someone else's

  • Are comfortable challenging unnecessary security bureaucracy and genuinely risky engineering decisions alike

  • Get frustrated when a security fix takes weeks instead of days

Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a $116 million Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

Our robots produce data no lab can stage. Our fleet has recorded more than 500 million manipulation interactions in live warehouse operations; Cortex 2.0 was trained on a curated 10 million of them and added a world model that plans before it acts (arXiv 2604.20246). Cortex 2.5 learns a new task from a few demonstrations instead of a training run. Deployments are growing from single robots to fleets, and the research team is growing with them.

We now want one scientific leader who owns the research behind Cortex end to end and turns what our fleet experiences every day into the next step change in what robots can do.

The Real-World Learning Loop is your system

Sereact is a frontier research lab and a production-grade robotics company in one. Our bet: general-purpose robotic intelligence “must be learned from live deployments” (The Real-World Learning Loop, Feb 2026). Every stage of that loop is yours to raise:

  • In-Situ Policy Execution. Every robot in production runs the current policy, and every shift is an experiment. You decide what the policies expose for learning.

  • Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own interactions while they work. You decide what is worth recording and which situations the fleet should go and find.

  • Data Curation and Learning. Novelty, uncertainty, failures and distribution shift decide what we learn from. You own the curation and the training recipe.

  • Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies pass validation gates before they return to the fleet. You set the bar, and how fast we can clear it safely.

Every deployment teaches the next one. Your job is to make that loop turn faster and teach more each time.

Responsibilities

  • Set the research agenda for Cortex: vision-language-action models, world models and planning, learning from interaction on real robots, and generalization across tasks and embodiments.

  • Make the big bets: which directions get people and compute, and which ones we stop.

  • Own the data strategy: the mix of deployment, teleoperation, open-source and synthetic data, and what the fleet collects next.

  • Own the compute strategy, from large-scale training to real-time inference on the robot.

  • Build the evaluation science: benchmarks that predict performance in a customer’s operation, not only on a leaderboard.

  • Build and lead the research organisation in Zurich and Stuttgart: structure, leads, rhythm.

  • Set the hiring bar and make Sereact the place the best people in robot learning want to join.

  • Take research into production with engineering, so results reach the fleet in weeks and hold up in 24/7 operation.

  • Decide with the founders what we publish, open-source or patent, and build our standing at CoRL, RSS, ICRA, NeurIPS and ICML.

  • Be Sereact’s scientific voice with customers, partners, universities and investors, and build academic partnerships.

  • Partner with the CTO, product and operations, so research, engineering and deployment pull in one direction.

Not in scope, by design

  • Software platform, hardware and field deployment engineering. They stay with the CTO and operations: the CTO owns how we build and ship, you own what we learn next.

  • A research lab beside the business. Research at Sereact ends on a robot, ideally at a customer.

  • Product roadmap and pricing.

What makes this role hard

  • Research and production compete for the same robots, people and compute. You make that trade-off every week, in the open.

  • Cortex is not a blank page. It already runs in customer operations, and our founders are deeply technical. You raise the ceiling of a running system.

  • A result counts when it holds up in a customer’s operation, not when the paper is accepted.

Your first 12 months

  • First 90 days: know the fleet, the data and the team; agree the research roadmap with the founders; one evaluation standard everyone uses.

  • By month 6: a research organisation with clear ownership and a release rhythm from experiment to fleet.

  • By month 12: a new generation of Cortex in customer operations with measurable gains, key senior hires made, and work that puts Sereact on the map of robot learning.

What you bring

  • You have led research in robot learning or embodied AI (VLA models, imitation or reinforcement learning, world models) and built a team around it.

  • Your work runs on real robots, ideally outside the lab and for long stretches. You know what breaks first.

  • You explain science to engineers, customers and investors alike, and you enjoy it.

  • PhD in machine learning, robotics or a related field, or an equivalent track record.

Nice to have: large-scale pretraining of foundation models · fleet learning or data engines · industrial manipulation · experience in both academia and industry.

Three questions we will ask you

  1. Tell us about a model you took from a paper to a robot that ran for weeks without you. What broke first?

  2. If you had our deployment data tomorrow, which bet would you make first, and what would you stop?

  3. How do you decide what to publish and what to keep?

How we hire

Conversations with both founders, a research deep dive with the team, and a working session on a real problem from our deployments. We move fast.

We are looking for a Senior Mechanical Systems Engineer (all genders) to help us design and develop the mechanical systems on board our fully battery-electric aircraft (CS-23). You will work closely with overall aircraft design, structures, flight physics, propulsion and other engineering teams to ensure optimal system integration and will play a key role in the detailed definition of the overall aircraft.

  • Perform system-level functional analysis, including functional decomposition and identification of system interfaces.

  • Define and manage functional and physical interfaces between mechanical systems and other aircraft disciplines.

  • Collaborate with partners and suppliers as a technical interface for mechanical systems.

  • Support Functional Hazard Assessments (FHA) and system safety activities in accordance with ARP4754A, ARP4761A and applicable certification requirements.

  • Support system integration, verification, testing and certification activities.

  • Engineering degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.

  • 8+ years of aerospace experience, with a focus on aircraft mechanical systems.

  • Experience with systems engineering, including requirements definition, functional analysis and system integration.

  • Knowledge and experience in mechanical aircraft systems, preferably cabin Environmental Control System and/or landing gear.

  • Own resolution of escalated, high-severity, or cross-system customer issues, providing clear and timely customer communication while balancing speed, technical quality, and customer impact.

title: Founding implementation strategist [ERP + AI]
description:
TL;DR

  • We're building the SAP/NetSuite of the AI era for mid-sized companies in the real-world economy, starting with their supply chain operations (buy, sell, stock, produce)

  • Founding deployment strategist: you deploy two things into real factories, in the same project, the ERP that runs their operations, and the AI agents that work inside it. Every client goes from signed contract to go-live on the date we promised, running on Piston, with agents already doing part of the work

  • A rare shape: someone who has led client projects that landed in industrial companies, who is genuinely AI-native, and who will write the deployment playbook for the team and our system integrator partners

  • €3M Pre-seed (Top-tier VCs)

What this role is (and isn't)

Most ERP deployments are people moving data around for a year. Incumbents quote six figures for it, and the client gets the same software they had, just newer. Ours run in eight to twelve weeks and deliver two things at once: a new ERP that runs buying, selling, stock and production, and AI agents inside it that read the orders, recompute the production load, prepare the purchases, and ask a human only when it matters.

This is not a product or a sales role, you are a deployment strategist. In one project, you replace a company's ERP and you put AI agents to work inside it.

Why now

Since day one, the founders have run every deployment themselves. Clients are now coming in faster than we can handle, and we need someone to own deployments. You work directly with Eric, CEO, who also leads product. That puts you as close as it gets to what success means at Piston: the success of our clients.

What you'll do

  • Deploy the ERP, with AI. The client's sales, purchasing, stock and production move onto Piston: data migrated from their old ERP and their Excel files, configuration built from their own documents, training, go-live. AI does the heavy lifting, you do the judgment.

  • Put the first AI agents live, during the ERP deployment. You decide what each agent does on its own, what it hands to a human for approval, and you make sure it's still running three months later.

  • Write the deployment playbook. Every go-live feeds a playbook that our next deployment hires and our system integrator partners will follow.

  • Map where the client's time goes. On site, you find the work that eats people's days: re-keying orders, chasing suppliers, rebuilding the same Excel every month. That map is the backlog of the next agents.

  • Teach humans to work with agents. The people you deploy with have never supervised software that acts on its own. You show them how to trust it, check it and correct it.

  • Hold the date and the budget. You size each deployment before the contract and protect that budget.

  • Use the tools engineers build for you. Our engineers build the tools that let you deploy on your own: AI-assisted data migration from the client's old ERP and Excel files, and a builder for screens and agents. You tell them what slows you down, they make it disappear.

  • Agentify your own work. On top of the tools our engineers build, you create your own agents for the deployment itself: configuration checks, test scenarios, training material, status reports. Every manual step you repeat twice becomes an agent for the next deployment.

What you bring

You bring the energy to deploy AI at scale in industrial companies. You learn fast from discovery, and you're as comfortable with founders and leadership teams as with operators on the shop floor.

Must have

  • Customer-facing project experience. Two years or more managing client projects in an industrial environment, typically in consulting (operations, supply chain, transformation). You've held deadlines, managed stakeholders, and delivered.

  • AI-native, for real. You use LLMs every day, and you've built things with them: automations, agents, prompts that run in production (Claude, GPT, n8n, Make, scripts, whatever works). You know what an agent can do alone, where it breaks, and where a human must stay in the loop.

  • Listening before configuring. You translate what people say into what the system and the agents must do, and you notice when the two don't match.

  • At ease in front of clients: Plant directors, finance, shop-floor operators. You can hold a room, and say no in it.

  • A full load, gladly. Around 150 project days a year, several deployments running at once.

  • Fluent English and French, both required. Our first clients work in French, our team writes in English, and you may support our deployments in the United States.

Nice to have

  • You've automated a real operations process end to end, with measurable hours saved

  • You've already taken a complex B2B software live

  • Comfortable with AI

  • You've worked around manufacturing or food operations: lots, BOMs, production orders, campaigns

  • Seed / Series A experience, where nobody's job description holds for long

Talent beats checklists. If you're intrigued, apply anyway.

How we'll measure success

  • ERP go-lives on the date we promised

  • Days spent against the plan we sold

  • Agents still running three months after launch, and the hours of work they take off the client's hands

What you'll get

  • World-class peers

  • The first hire of our deployment team: you write the playbook that future hires and our system integrator partners will follow, and you grow with the team it builds

  • A front-row seat on how AI agents change the way real companies operate

  • Regular company offsite (2–4 times per year) in great locations

  • Ideal equipment and setup

  • Remote-first (France), about 20% of your time on client sites

Process

We value efficiency and clarity. The entire process takes no more than 2 weeks:

  1. 30-minute intro call with Florian (CRO)

  2. 60-minute deployment deep dive with Eric (CEO)

  3. 30-min cultural-fit interview with Eugène (CTO)

  4. 2 days paid assessment, on a real client situation.

  5. Offer: If it's a match, we move fast.

Interested? Tell us about a client project you led, and something you automated with AI. A short, personal note goes a long way, AI-generated cover letters don't.
